**Job Title: Senior Hardware Manager - Digital Systems**

**Job Code: EEM6**

**Job Location: Carlsbad, California**

**Job Schedule: 9/80: Employees work 9 out of every 14 days- totaling 80 hours worked- and have every other Friday off**

**Job Description:**

Lead the FPGA and digital-hardware engineering function for complex Tactical Data Links systems, including architecture, design, development, modification, evaluation, integration, verification, and production execution. Set technical vision and execution priorities while coordinating personnel, lab resources, tools, and cross-functional support across wireless digital communications, modems, networking, digital signal processing, and electronic-warfare applications.Lead, develop, and retain a high-performing team of FPGA and digital-hardware engineers through clear priorities, regular coaching, performance management, and career-development planning. Build the organization’s technical bench by hiring strategically, mentoring emerging leaders, and aligning individual assignments with program needs and growth opportunities. Foster a culture of accountability, collaboration, inclusion, andcontinuous improvement while ensuring workload, staffing, and technical resources are balanced across programs and priorities.

**Essential Functions:**

- Lead architecture, design, development, modification, evaluation, integration, and production support for FPGA and digital-hardware systems, components, and integrated circuitry.

- Create technical vision, strategy, staffing plans, and execution priorities for the FPGA and digital-hardware team.

- Coordinate personnel, laboratory resources, tools, and technical support required for programs, proposals, pursuits, IRAD, development, integration, production, and sustaining work.

- Direct technical, schedule, and cost performance for FPGA and digital-hardware scope; review key technical decisions, deliverables, estimates, risks, and corrective actions.

- Guide the full design lifecycle from proposals and requirements definition through coding, simulation, synthesis, place and route, verification, test, and transition to production.

- Lead analysis, test, debug, and evaluation activities that establish operating data, validate designs, and resolve technical risks.

- Set design approaches, staffing priorities, and technical parameters based on electrical requirements, feasibility, schedule, cost, reliability, and long-term sustainability.

- Lead, mentor, develop, and retain engineers and technical leaders; align workforce capability and resources with business priorities.

- Build a culture of innovation, accountability, transparency, collaboration, and continuous improvement while influencing engineering leaders, customers, suppliers, and cross-functional partners.

- Partner with systems, software, RF, mechanical, manufacturing, test, program management, and business development to align technology roadmaps, proposals, execution, and customer commitments.

- Active or obtainable Secret security clearance.

**Qualifications:**

- Bachelor's degree with a minimum of 12 years of prior related experience, graduate degree with a minimum of 10 years of prior related experience, or in lieu of a degree a minimum of 16 years of prior related experience.

**Preferred Additional Skills:**

- Strong root-cause analysis, technical judgment, and decision-making across multiple functions or business areas.

- Experience with VHDL or Verilog and implementation of complex modem or DSP circuits in programmable logic; comparable ASIC experience is applicable.

- Experience with discrete-time DSP, digital communications, high-speed DSP data paths, digital filters, FFTs, error-correction codes, Turbo or LDPC, modulation, demodulation, and forward-error correction.

- Experience with high-speed serial interfaces, Ethernet, SPI, UART, SDRAM, DDR, JESD, PCIe, memory controllers, and software-to-FPGA interfaces.

- Experience with laboratory debug techniques using digital scopes, logic analyzers, BERTs, and other complex measurement devices.

- Working knowledge of testbench architectures, MATLAB, SystemC, C, or C++; ability to read, understand, and review schematic drawings.

- Experience with Git, Bitbucket, JIRA, and disciplined configuration management.

- Experience translating strategy into clear priorities, staffing plans, technical roadmaps, and execution outcomes.

- Experience leading cross-functional engineering teams and providing compelling technical briefings to senior leaders.

- Broad management and cross-functional leadership knowledge with mastery in digital design, electrical engineering, or closely related technical areas.

- Demonstrated experience leading experienced professionals, supervisors, or managers in a complex technical environment.

- Strong background indigital design, analysis, integration, simulation, synthesis, verification, test, evaluation, and production support for complex hardware systems.

- Experience with wireless digital communications, modems, networking, digital signal processing, electronic warfare, or comparable high-performance digital systems.

- Ability to communicate and influence leadership regarding matters of substantial importance to the function or business area.

**Job Title: Senior Associate, Program Data Management / Configuration Management (Sign-On Bonus Available)**

**Job Code: 45050**

**Job Location: Palm Bay, Florida**

**Job Schedule: 9/80: Employees work 9 out of every 14 days – totaling 80 hours worked, and have every other Friday off**

**Job Description:**

We're looking for a Senior Associate, Configuration Data Management to join our team in Palm Bay, Florida. In this role, you'll be responsible for managing all the important product data and technical documentation for our program. You'll make sure information is properly identified, collected, prepared, controlled, shared, and archived so the right people get what they need when they need it.

If you're highly organized and have experience entering data into systems accurately, you can do this job. You don't need a configuration management background to be successful here. Whether you've worked in data entry, document control, administrative support, or any role where attention to detail and organization were critical, those skills translate directly to this position. You'll be supporting engineering and program management teams with their data and documentation needs, coordinating deliverables, and keeping everything running smoothly. If you're someone who thrives on keeping things organized, meeting deadlines, and ensuring accuracy, this role is a great fit.

**Essential Functions:**

- CDRL/SDRL Management – Ensure contract deliverables are provided to the customer on time, complies with Contract Statements of Work, requirements, policies, procedures, plans, program schedules, and other technical documentation. Maintain the delivery schedule and coordinate with program team members to provide input and communicate deadlines
- Documentation Formatting – Ensure program documentation adheres to internal standards, formatting requirements, and contract authorization. Ensure correct and complete markings on all documentation. Apply and track control numbers or other identifiers as required
- Data Handling and Transfer – Manage all communication (incoming and outgoing) with the customer, log and track messages, maintain folder structures, facilitate the transfer of data between different networks and systems, media burning, file scanning, and file uploading.
- Data Entry – Input data into configuration management tool systems, ensure complete and accurate records, facilitate the correction of any errors or missing data
- Other – Provide other functional support as assigned to assist the execution of various engineering and program management activities. Willing to work overtime and/or outside of normal business hours as needed to meet deadlines


**Qualifications:**

- Active TS/SCI with Polygraph clearance required (elevated Poly)

- Bachelor’s Degree and a minimum of 2 years of prior related experience. Graduate Degree or equivalent with 0 to 2 years of prior related experience. In lieu of a degree, minimum of 6 years of prior related experience


**Preferred Additional Skills:**

- Professional experience using Microsoft Office Suite (Word, Excel, PowerPoint, Outlook) and Visio
- Professional experience interpreting PDF documents and utilizing database systems
- Experience in using Configuration Management tools (Agile PLM, Confluence, Windchill or similar)
- Experience reading and interpreting Statements of Work and Data Item Description
- Experience in continuous process improvement techniques such as Lean Six Sigma

Data and AI Engineering Associate (8+ months preferred)

Company Description:

FluidAI is specialized in the development and deployment of data-driven surgical solutions, with an initial focus on general and gastrointestinal surgery. Our technologies integrate medical devices, software, and artificial intelligence into platforms that address real clinical and operational challenges across the continuum of surgical care.

We combine continuous physiological monitoring from our proprietary sensors with comprehensive electronic health record data, creating intelligent systems that enable earlier identification of clinical deterioration and complications. Beyond patient monitoring, our platform extends to patient education and engagement tools, as well as automated documentation and coding modules — supporting care teams and driving operational efficiency.

Our team brings together expertise across clinical practice, research, engineering, data science, manufacturing, and commercialization. We build solutions designed for real-world impact, supported by full in-house capabilities, a strong intellectual property portfolio, and partnerships with leading institutions around the world.

We are an equal opportunity employer and have a diverse team representation across language, ethnicity, gender and nationality.

Why Join FluidAI Medical?

  • Mission to save lives and improve patient care with technology that’s already deployed on patients in real-world settings.
  • Work with a high-performing and cross-functional team that is empowered to grow, learn, and contribute across all levels of the organization.
  • Personal career-focused development and training with access to workshops, coursework, and experienced mentors/consultants.
  • Regular offsite activities – past events include rafting, axe-throwing, sports leagues, and regular BBQs.

Job Summary:

This role centers around extracting clinical value from data produced by our proprietary sensors and systems (and beyond) to improve patient outcomes. We're looking for someone with solid foundations in software architecture and development to work with our Software Led Team to deliver high quality products.

It's not everyday that you get a chance to make a direct impact on people's health. If you're looking to join a strong team for a meaningful product, this is for you!

Note: This is an office-first role working out of our Kitchener HQ in the Medical Innovation Xchange

Job Responsibilities:

  • Update, design and implement mobile and cloud architecture to enable patient data collection and processing, and presentation of results to healthcare professionals
  • Translate regulatory requirements (e.g., HIPA, PHIPA) to product specifications and ensure compliance
  • Devise deployment strategy for local and international hospitals depending on their infrastructure and IT policies.
  • Assist in conducting technical risk and privacy impact assessments.
  • Support other teams with software needs as required.

Qualifications:

These are some of the skills we are looking for in an ideal candidate.

  • Demonstrated knowledge of backend architecture design and implications on development, security, and privacy
  • Strong knowledge of data structures and database fundamentals
  • Strong knowledge of back-end development (C# Preferred) Strong Knowledge of mobile software development (Android (Kotlin & Java) preferred)
  • Good knowledge UX design for website and mobile development Ability to work with a multidisciplinary set of teams
  • Excellent written and verbal technical communication skills
  • Ability to work in a high-pressure environment and constantly changing conditions
  • Familiarity with version-control software (Git preferred)
  • Understanding of international regulatory pertaining to patient data security and privacy (HIPA, PHIPA), preferred
  • Knowledge of standard encryption algorithms for data security, preferred
  • Optional skills: Python

Transparency & Hiring Practices:

  • Compensation : The pay for this position will be based on average co-op wages as outlined by your academic institution’s co-op program or similar institutions if specific data is unavailable, ensuring fair and competitive compensation aligned with industry and academic standards. The typical range for this role is $22 - $25 per hour for work terms 2-4.
  • Grant Eligibility : This position is made possible through wage subsidy grants such as BioTalent SWPP. As such, participants must be a current student, registered in a Canadian Post-secondary program. International students are not eligible. Eligible participants must be a Canadian citizen, permanent resident or person who has been granted refugee status in Canada and be legally entitled to work.
  • Co-op Requirement : As this is a co-op position, candidates must have a co-op work term scheduled with their university for the term they are applying for.
  • Application Screening : All applications are screened manually. We do not use AI or AI-Augmented Applicant Tracking Systems (ATS) to screen, assess, reject, or select candidates.
  • Position Status : This winter term position will become available in Winter 2027.

title: Asset Protection Detective, Queens Center - Full Time
description:
Be Part of an Amazing Story

Macy’s is more than just a store. We’re a story. One that’s captured the hearts and minds of America for more than 160 years. A story about innovations and traditions…about inspiring stores and irresistible products…about the excitement of the Macy’s 4th of July Fireworks, and the wonder of the Thanksgiving Day Parade. We’ve been part of memorable moments and milestones for countless customers and colleagues. Those stories are part of what makes this such a special place to work.

Job Overview

As an Asset Protection Detective, you will help protect company assets, reduce shortage, and support a safe, customer-focused shopping environment. Using surveillance, investigative tools, and strong partnerships with store teams and law enforcement, you will identify and respond to theft, recover merchandise, and help protect our customers, colleagues, and business.

Why This Role Matters

Asset Protection Detectives play an important role in reducing loss while maintaining a safe and welcoming store environment. Through training, observation, investigation, and de-escalation, this role helps protect company assets, support colleagues, and ensure customers can shop with confidence.

How Our Asset Protection Colleagues Spend Their Day…

  • Our colleagues begin each day energized and ready to make an impact. They greet teammates with a warm hello. Before they get started, they review updates and department information so they're fully informed and ready to engage with confidence.

  • We believe service starts with each other - supporting one another with honesty, care, and collaboration so we can better serve our customers and communities.

  • And we know that excellence is a journey - we strive to improve every day, take pride in our work, achieve sales goals and learn from each other to deliver individual and store results.

Full-time colleagues are typically scheduled to work 30 or more hours per week, while part-time colleagues are typically scheduled 12-24 hours per week. All schedules contain weekend shifts as part of the requirements. Hours are dependent on business needs and colleague availability. Information regarding hours per week needed for benefit eligibility purposes can be found here.

What To Expect

  • Use surveillance techniques, investigative tools, and reporting systems to help identify theft, dishonest activity, and shortage trends.

  • Partner with Asset Protection leaders, store teams, and law enforcement to support investigations and protect company assets.

  • Apply de-escalation tools and sound judgment to help maintain a safe environment for customers and colleagues.

  • Prepare clear documentation, statements, and evidence to support investigations, audits, and legal proceedings.

  • Support team readiness by training colleagues on protocols that help protect company assets.

How You’ll Make an Impact

  • Help protect customers, colleagues, and company assets by identifying, investigating, and responding to theft and dishonest activity.

  • Use surveillance techniques to support the apprehension of shoplifters and dishonest employees, while following company policies and legal requirements.

  • Recover stolen merchandise and provide statements, evidence, and documentation to support investigations.

  • Prepare timely and accurate reports related to theft incidents, investigations, audits, and assigned activities.

  • Build strong partnerships with store colleagues, Asset Protection leaders, and law enforcement to support investigations and shortage reduction.

  • Maintain compliance with company policies and legal standards related to apprehensions, searches, and evidence preservation.

  • Testify in court for criminal and civil cases, as needed.

  • Respond to alarm calls, support special assignments, and facilitate first aid for customers and colleagues when needed.

  • Foster an environment of acceptance and respect that strengthens relationships with colleagues, customers, and communities.

Skills That Matter

Must Have

  • Ability to observe, identify, and respond to suspicious activity in a retail environment.

  • Strong communication skills with the ability to partner effectively with customers, colleagues, leaders, and law enforcement.

  • Ability to use sound judgment, de-escalation tools, and company procedures to support a safe environment.

  • Ability to handle proprietary, sensitive, and confidential information with discretion and integrity.

  • For jobs in New York, a current New York State Security Guard License is required.

Nice to Have

  • Experience in retail, customer service, asset protection, security, investigations, or law enforcement.

  • Ability to prepare accurate reports, statements, and documentation related to incidents and investigations.

  • Experience using surveillance systems, reporting tools, or investigative technology.

  • Ability to train or coach colleagues on asset protection protocols, shortage reduction, or safety practices.

Physical Activities You Will Perform

  • This role involves performing essential job functions such as communication, collaboration, and use of office and computer systems. title: Data Center Engineer
description:
Job Description:

Role Overview

We are hiring a Datacenter Engineer to support the mission critical infrastructure that powers our markets, market data services and member connectivity responsible from all aspects of Cboe’s datacenter physical footprint. This is a hands-on role responsible for installing, maintaining, and troubleshooting all datacenter hardware, cabling, and supporting infrastructure across our colocation facilities.

This role is ideal for someone who is detail oriented, organized, comfortable in datacenter settings, and eager to grow within a highly reliable, mission critical environment and experienced performing largescale MAC (Moves, Adds, Changes) activities. You will collaborate regularly with Engineering, Operations, and NOC teams.

Please note: Candidate selected for this role must be willing to work on site at our Chicago, Illinois area Data Centers.

Shift Requirements

This role will require you to be available for the following late shift schedule, which is subject to change. This is a 2nd shift position, Tuesday through Saturday. The role follows a 5-day, 8-hour workweek, with shifts scheduled between Tuesday and Saturday. Standard 2nd shift hours are 2:00pm to 11pm.

US Holiday coverage may be required.

Please note: The role may be eligible for a shift differential of 10% depending on the shift worked.

In this role, you will be responsible for:

  • Install and maintain servers, network devices, storage systems, and associated cabling and cross connectivity

  • Perform structured cabling (copper, MMF, SMF), including testing, routing, labeling, and documentation

  • Execute daily MAC tasks including equipment installs, moves, and rack/cable upgrades

  • Be our hands and eyes in the data center and report any environmental issues (power, cooling, temperatures) and escalate to management and the provider

  • Work with Engineering and NOC teams to troubleshoot hardware, application and connectivity issues directly and via Jira tickets

  • Generate and maintain equipment inventories, rack elevations, cable maps, and documentation standards

  • Respond to datacenter incidents including hardware failures and cabling issues

  • Support new equipment rollouts and datacenter expansion projects

  • Assist with vendor coordination, shipping/receiving, RMAs, and onsite service activities

  • Support the ongoing development and improvement of our global datacenter operations standards

  • Participate in on-call coverage and shift rotations

  • Research new Data Center infrastructure equipment advancements and recommend changes as needed to management

  • Demonstrated ability to deliver high-quality, consistent, reliable work and a strong sense of ownership in supporting critical operations

The ideal candidate will have:

  • 5+ years’ experience in datacenter support including:

  • Racking, removing, cabling and troubleshooting server, storage, and network equipment in colocation environment

  • MAC work which includes installing/moving equipment and cabling on a large-scale basis

  • The candidate will need to be proficient in cable plant design and troubleshooting (Copper/MMF/SMF) as well as proficient in the industry standard testing tools

  • Basic working knowledge of HVAC, power, fire, building security systems operations, and safety

  • Working knowledge of telecommunications technologies, systems, and circuits

  • Ability to lift up to 75 lbs and work inside datacenter environments for extended periods

  • Ability to work independently and manage multiple tasks and projects

  • Ability to work well in a dynamic team-oriented environment

  • Excellent written and verbal communication skills with a strong attention to detail

  • Ability to multitask and manage multiple projects

  • Team player, desiring to be part of a high-performance team with dynamic responsibilities

  • Perform other duties as assigned by management

  • Must be willing and flexible to work different shifts (as needed to support the business needs) for short-to-long-term periods of time as well as participate in the On Call support rotation


This position is not eligible for visa sponsorship. Candidates must be legally authorized to work in the United States without the need for employer sponsorship now or in the future.

Salary Ranges (applicable for US locations only)

At Cboe, we are committed to providing a competitive, transparent, and market‑informed total rewards program. The anticipated base salary range for this role is $102,850-$133,100, with actual compensation determined by job‑related factors such as skills, relevant experience, education, internal alignment, and location.

This role may also be eligible for annual incentive compensation and, where applicable, participation in Cboe's long-term equity programs.

Additional information about Cboe's total rewards program, including benefits and other compensation components, can be found here: Total Rewards at CBOE.​

title: Lead, Cyber Incident Response
description:
Sony Pictures Entertainment (SPE) is seeking an experienced Lead Cyber Incident Response professional to help protect the company's people, intellectual property, productions, technology platforms, and business operations from cyber threats.


This role leads complex cybersecurity investigations, coordinates response activities during significant security incidents, and advances SPE's incident response capabilities. The successful candidate will serve as a senior technical resource within the Incident Response team, leading investigations across corporate, cloud, identity, SaaS, and production environments while partnering with Security Operations, Threat Intelligence, Engineering, Legal, Privacy, People & Organization (P&O), Corporate Communications, and business stakeholders.


Key Responsibilities

  • Incident Response and Investigations

    • Lead complex cybersecurity investigations from initial detection through containment, eradication, recovery, and post-incident review.
    • Serve as incident commander for assigned incidents, coordinating technical responders and business stakeholders throughout the response lifecycle.
    • Investigate ransomware, identity compromise, phishing, insider threats, data exposure, cloud security incidents, and other advanced cyber threats.
    • Conduct digital forensic investigations to determine root cause, scope, business impact, and remediation requirements.

  • Business and Asset Protection

    • Investigate threats affecting SPE intellectual property, content, productions, employees, technology platforms, third-party partners, and business operations.
    • Assess cyber events from both technical and business-risk perspectives, balancing risk reduction with operational continuity.
    • Partner with Legal, Privacy, People & Organization (P&O), Corporate Communications, and business leadership on sensitive investigations and response activities.

  • Security Operations and Continuous Improvement

    • Collaborate with Security Operations, Threat Intelligence, Detection Engineering, and Security Engineering to enhance detection and response capabilities.
    • Develop and improve incident response playbooks, runbooks, escalation procedures, investigative methodologies, and operational standards.
    • Drive automation and workflow optimization through SOAR, scripting, AI-enabled capabilities, and emerging technologies.
    • Lead post-incident reviews and translate lessons learned into measurable security and operational improvements.

  • Technical Leadership

    • Serve as a senior escalation point for complex investigations and high-severity incidents.
    • Mentor Incident Response analysts through case reviews, training, coaching, and knowledge sharing.
    • Provide clear technical updates, executive-ready summaries, after-action reports, and risk-informed recommendations.
    • Contribute to strategic initiatives that strengthen SPE cyber resilience and operational maturity.

Qualifications

Required

  • 8+ years of cybersecurity experience, with significant focus on incident response, digital forensics, threat hunting, or security operations.
  • Proven experience leading enterprise-scale cybersecurity investigations and incident response efforts.
  • Strong knowledge of modern attack techniques, threat actor behavior, digital forensics, and investigative methodologies.
  • Experience with cloud security, identity security, endpoint detection and response (EDR/XDR), SIEM, and SOAR platforms.
  • Excellent analytical, communication, and stakeholder-management skills, including the ability to explain complex technical issues to executive and non-technical audiences.

Preferred

  • Experience supporting global media, entertainment, technology, or other highly distributed enterprise environments.
  • Experience investigating incidents involving intellectual property, insider threats, data exposure, or third-party compromise.
  • Experience with Microsoft 365, Azure, AWS, modern SaaS environments, and identity platforms.
  • Knowledge of Python, PowerShell, or other scripting and automation technologies.
  • Relevant industry certifications such as CISSP, GCIH, GCFA, GCIA, GNFA, or equivalent.

The anticipated base salary for this position is $142,400 - $178,000. This role may also qualify for annual incentive and/or comprehensive benefits. The actual base salary offered will depend on a variety of factors, including without limitation, the qualifications of the individual applicant for the position, years of relevant experience, level of education attained, certifications or other professional licenses held, and if applicable, the location of the position.

Sony Pictures Entertainment is an equal opportunity employer. We evaluate qualified applicants without regard to race, color, religion, sex, national origin, disability, veteran status, age, sexual orientation, gender identity, or other protected characteristics.

SPE will consider qualified applicants with arrest or conviction records in accordance with applicable law.

If recording or the use of the tools occurs during the interview and cannot be promptly turned off or disabled, the interviewer may end the interview.

title: Regulatory Specialist
description:

At Flourish Research, we strive toward excellence. In clinical trials and healthcare, excellence means everyone deserves the best care, regardless of their race, color, gender identity, religion, ethnicity, physical abilities, age, sexual orientation, or veteran status. The more diversity we have in our team, the more unique perspectives, and ideas we share, and the better prepared we are to serve our communities. WE SEE YOU. WE ARE YOU. WE EMBRACE YOU. WE CELEBRATE YOU!

Flourish Research is looking for motivated, talented, creative individuals who want to learn and grow in their careers while contributing to research that changes lives! We offer an excellent comprehensive benefits package, a supportive and collaborative work environment, and endless growth opportunities.

About the Job:

We are actively hiring a Regulatory Specialist to support our Walnut Creek, CA site.

Shift: Monday-Friday day shift (40 hours per week)
Location: Onsite, Walnut Creek, CA
FLSA Classification: Non-Exempt
Compensation: $25 to $27 per hour (depending on experience)

PURPOSE: To create, maintain and coordinate regulatory documents and activities throughout clinical research studies conducted by a Flourish Research site according to Flourish Research's SOPs, policies and procedures, applicable federal regulations, medical ethics, International Council of Harmonization (ICH), Good Clinical Practices (GCPs), Institutional Review Board (IRB) requirements, and in compliance with specific sponsor protocol requirements. To work closely with site leadership, principal investigators, and site staff. To collaborate with Sponsors, CROs, and IRB staff. Role functions begin at the time of study start-up, continuing through the duration of the trial, and until after study is deemed closed. All responsibilities should be completed in accordance with Flourish Research's Core Values and Employee Manual.

Additionally, a Regulatory Specialist will be primarily focused on study start-up, delegation and training. We are seeing increased complexity and volume of protocol start-up requirements and regulatory tasks. We need additional on-site support to drive start-up processes. title: Research Assistant
description:
Valkyrie Clinical Trials (VCT), a Flourish Research Company, is a leading Oncology multi-site clinical research network with expertise in Oncology research. VCT approaches clinical research with a deep sense of humanity, compassion, and sincere kindness. VCT was founded by leading Clinical Oncologist, Dr. David Berz, and has multiple sites spanning California in Century City, Panaroma City, and Murrieta, and has recently expanded to Denver, Colorado.

Flourish Research is one of the industry’s most progressive and diversified clinical trial organizations, with strong capabilities across cardiology, metabolic disorders, renal, oncology, CNS, pulmonology, and vaccine research. At Flourish Research, we strive toward excellence. In clinical trials and healthcare, excellence means everyone deserves the best care, regardless of their race, color, gender identity, religion, ethnicity, physical abilities, age, sexual orientation, or veteran status. We embrace employees, customers, and patients from these underrepresented groups to help make this vision a reality. Flourish is committed to a safe work environment where all employees, customers, and patients are included, and treated with dignity and respect. The more diversity we have in our team, the more unique perspectives, and ideas we share, and the better prepared we are to serve our communities. WE SEE YOU. WE ARE YOU. WE EMBRACE YOU. WE CELEBRATE YOU!


We are actively hiring a Research Assistant to support our Valkyrie Clinical Trials Denver, Colorado site.

LOCATION: Onsite, Denver, Colorado
FLSA: Non-Exempt
HOURS: Monday to Friday, Day Shift, 40 hours per week
COMPENSATION: $25-$28 per hour (depending on experience)

The Research Assistant (RA) supports the activities, duties, and procedures required for the start-up, conduct, and close-out of oncology clinical trial protocols at Valkyrie Clinical Trials. Working under the direction of a Clinical Research Coordinator (CRC) or Team Lead, the role helps obtain clean, objective, and accurate data within sponsor timelines while protecting participant safety and maintaining inspection-ready documentation.

Two things distinguish this role beyond standard clinical support. Oncology protocols are clinically dense, so building real familiarity with the state of the disease, treatment history, and clinical rationale behind each assigned protocol, not just the task list, is part of the job from day one. In this patient population, a missed detail is a safety issue before it's ever a data issue. Valkyrie's care model is also white glove. Participants and their families are never routed around or told no when they hit a logistical obstacle, and the RA is expected to help remove those barriers, escalating to the CRC or Team Lead when a resolution is beyond their current scope.

This is the individual contributor entry point into the Clinical Research Coordinator job family. The band spans Research Assistants who are new to clinical research through Senior Research Assistants operating with greater independence and taking on more complex protocol responsibilities. Progression through the band, and eventual readiness for the CRC role, is determined by the Flourish Research CRC Competency Assessment.

All work is performed in accordance with Flourish Research SOPs, policies and procedures, federal regulations, medical ethics, Good Clinical Practice, ICH guidelines, IRB requirements, sponsor protocol requirements, and the Flourish Research Core Values, Mission Statement, and Employee Manual.

Essential Job Functions:

A. Read and understand protocols to help accomplish protocol-specified patient visits and procedures as directed by assigned Team Lead or CRC.

B. Under the direction of assigned Team Lead or CRC and after completion of required training, clearly and concisely document patient assessments, observations, test results, and other study-related information per federal regulations, protocol requirements, and GCPs.

C. Obtain patient informed consent according to federal regulations, GCPs, and IRB requirements.

D. Assist in the creative and diligent recruitment of qualified study subjects into assigned protocols to fulfill enrollment obligations within the sponsor's timeline while following regulations and rules governing medical ethics, IRB, and GCP guidelines.

E. Assist in the scheduling, preparation, and conducting of patient visits according to protocol requirements and timelines as directed by assigned Team Lead or CRC.

F. Under close supervision, maintain accurate and complete written source documentation of patient visits and protocol-related activities.

G. Accurately complete case report forms (CRFs) and/or worksheets generated by the sponsor or CRO.

H. Maintain confidentiality of patient and/or protocol issues as appropriate and as bound by Confidentiality Agreements, including but not limited to those with Flourish Research, between Flourish Research and sponsors, and between Flourish Research and other entities.

I. Promptly report adverse events to the Team Lead, CRC, or other supervisor and/or Principal Investigator/Sub-Investigator as deemed necessary.

J. Assist in the accountability of clinical trial materials (i.e., CRFs, study drug, lab supplies, and/or other required items) and help ensure availability of appropriate quantities required for the study.

K. Maintain ongoing communication with the Team Lead, CRC, Clinical Team Manager, Principal Investigator, and other persons assisting with the study, and document these communications according to protocol requirements and Flourish Research policies.

L. Attend required training courses/conferences to stay current and aware of changing federal regulations and Flourish Research policies.

M. Pursue educational opportunities to increase knowledge of the research process and associated rules and regulations governing clinical research.

N. Perform all study-related duties in a time- and cost-effective manner in adherence with Flourish policies.

O. Perform all duties in a safe and prudent manner.

P. Represent Flourish Research in a professional and courteous manner (verbal, written, and in appearance) when interacting with Flourish staff, sponsors, IRBs, patients/subjects, and nursing and medical staff members of various clinics, hospitals, and physicians' offices.

Q. Additional duties as assigned by management.

PHYSICAL JOB REQUIREMENTS:

A. Work is normally performed in a typical interior/office work environment.

B. Local travel may be required.

C. Exposure to human bodily fluids.

D. Laboratory processing procedures.

E. Participant care.

F. Extensive computer use.

G. Ability to properly lift thirty-five pounds and occasionally more than thirty-five pounds.

H. Occasional night and weekend work schedules.

I. Ability to drive and daily availability of an automobile.

Requirements

MINIMUM REQUIREMENTS:

Education: Bachelor's degree in a life sciences major preferred (i.e. Biology, Nursing, Healthcare Administration or related field), or equivalent experience in clinical research.

Experience: Preferably a minimum of 1-3+ years' experience within the field of clinical research or biological research. Oncology clinical research experience is a plus.

Knowledge and Skills:

● Exceptional knowledge of clinical research methods.

● Demonstrates core values and all skills set required.

● Demonstrated ability to collaborate and align with all research department teams.

● Excellent oral and written communication skills.

● Excellent computer skills to include Office 365 products.

● Is moral and ethical in decision-making and during interaction with patients, sponsor and IRB representatives, physicians and staff at satellite clinics, and other employees.

● Must be professional, have a strong work ethic, be motivated to identify tasks that need to be completed, and strive for accuracy and quality when completing assignments.

● ECG, phlebotomy skills, and any other technical skills related to the completion of a study visit as required by the protocol.

● Must be able to adapt and take on additional tasks as requested.

● Assists with key initiatives/process improvements in the department.

● Assists with training company new hires.

● Completes at least 80% of goals annually.

Benefits

Health, dental, and vision insurance plans, 401(k) with a 100% employer match on the first 4% of employee contributions, tuition reimbursement, parental leave, employee referral program, employee assistance program, life insurance, disability insurance, and a generous PTO plan covering vacation, sick, personal days and 8 paid holidays.

title: Tornhuset søger social- og sundhedsassistent til aftenvagter i Tvillingehuset
description:
Er du en passioneret og engageret social- og sundhedsassistent, der ønsker at skabe udvikling og udfordre os med nye perspektiver, gode spørgsmål og dit eget faglige blik, så har vi måske den perfekte stilling til dig.

Hvad indebærer arbejdet?
Vores SSA beskriver den sundhedsfaglige opgave sådan:
”Som SSA i Tvillingehuset er du en vigtig del af borgernes hverdag. Du har et stort medansvar for borgernes sundhedsfaglige velbefindende i et tæt samarbejde med borgeren, pårørende, kolleger samt eksterne samarbejdspartnere (læger, psykiater og øvrige samarbejdspartnere)”

Vores faglige koordinator beskriver den pædagogiske opgave sådan:
”Vi møder det enkelte menneske med respekt for ønsker, drømme og retten til selv- og medbestemmelse. Gennem nærvær, anerkendelse og en forudsigelig og struktureret hverdag, arbejder vi for at borgerne oplever sig set, hørt og forstået. Når hverdagen bliver udfordrende, skaber vi tryghed og finder sammen med borgeren strategier, der understøtter mestring og handlemuligheder.”

Du bliver en del af borgernes hverdag og støtter dem i alt fra personlig pleje og struktur til aktiviteter, relationer og kommunikation.
Struktur og forudsigelighed er vigtige elementer i vores autismepædagogiske praksis. Men vi ved, at det gode liv også består af oplevelser, fællesskab og de muligheder, der opstår undervejs. Derfor skal du kunne være med til både at skabe trygge rammer og være fleksibel, når borgerens behov eller situationen kalder på noget andet.

Faglighed, udvikling og samarbejde
Vi er en tværfaglig medarbejdergruppe bestående af blandt andre pædagoger, ergoterapeuter, socialrådgivere, social- og sundhedsassistenter, omsorgsmedhjælpere, faglig koordinator og planlægger.
Vi arbejder løbende med at udvikle vores praksis gennem supervision, faglig sparring, LA2U og ASK. Vi tror på, at forskellige faglige perspektiver gør os klogere, og vi forventer, at du både bringer din egen faglighed i spil og er åben for andres input.

Hos os er du ansat til to ting: faglighed og samarbejde.

De bedste løsninger opstår oftest i dialogen på tværs af fagligheder, og når samarbejdet fungerer, kan det mærkes både hos borgerne og i arbejdsmiljøet. Vi forventer ikke, at vi altid er enige. Til gengæld forventer vi, at vi er nysgerrige på hinandens perspektiver, tager fat i det, der er svært, og holder fast i det fælles mål: at skabe de bedste rammer for borgernes trivsel, udvikling og livskvalitet.

Hvem er vi?
Tvillingehuset er en del af Tornhuset, som er et specialiseret autismetilbud i Odense Kommune.
Vi arbejder rehabiliterende med fokus på trivsel, deltagelse samt selv- og medbestemmelse.
I Tvillingehuset bor 14 mennesker mellem 29 og 68 år. De har forskellige personligheder, interesser, behov og måder at være i verden på. Fælles for dem er, at de har autisme, og flere har et lavt til middel funktionsniveau. Borgerne har i varierende grad behov for støtte til blandt andet personlig pleje og hygiejne, struktur i hverdagen, kommunikation og deltagelse i daglige aktiviteter.
Flere af borgerne er nonverbale eller kommunikerer på andre måder end gennem talesprog.
Et blik, en bevægelse eller en ændring i adfærd kan være vigtig information i arbejdet med borgeren.

Vi søger dig, der

  • Kan anvende dine faglige kompetencer i et tværfagligt samarbejde om hver enkelt borgers rehabiliteringsforløb.
  • Kan være tovholder på sundhedsfaglige problemstillinger og sikre kvaliteten i pleje og behandling
  • Kan tage medansvar for, at dine kollegaer er velinformerede om medicinsk behandling, virkninger og bivirkninger

description:
Position Summary: Responsibilities include any of the following activities related to the receiving, storing, and/or shipping of materials or finished goods: ensures materials are received from proper vendors, that they are delivered to inventory, and that finished goods are packaged according to specification and shipped in a timely manner. Reviews receipt of all materials to ensure purchase orders are open and the quality of materials received is correct.   • Unpacks and examines incoming shipments, rejects damaged items, records shortages, and corresponds with shipper to rectify damages and shortages.

  • Routes items to departments.

  • Examines outgoing shipments to ensure shipments meet specifications.

title: Data & Automation Specialist
description:
Data & Automation Specialist - Business Improvement & AI

Location: Magheralin
Working arrangement: On-site, five days per week
Reporting to: Operations Director

An established Northern Ireland business is looking to appoint a Data & Automation Specialist as part of continued investment in its systems, data and wider digital transformation.

This is a newly focused role sitting at the intersection of data, business improvement, automation and AI. You will work directly with the Operations Director and stakeholders across the organisation to identify inefficient processes and deliver practical technology-led improvements.

This is not purely a reporting or data analyst position. The focus is on understanding how the business operates and then using Power BI, SQL, automation and emerging AI tools to make it work better.



The role

You will work across finance, operations and other business functions to understand existing processes, identify areas of manual effort and determine where technology can make a measurable difference.

That could mean replacing a spreadsheet-heavy process with an automated workflow, improving the quality of operational reporting, building a Power BI dashboard or identifying a practical use case for AI.

You will have ownership from initial requirements gathering and process analysis through to building or coordinating the solution, testing it and supporting users through implementation.



Key responsibilities

  • Work with stakeholders across the business to understand processes, challenges and areas for improvement.
  • Review and document existing workflows and translate business requirements into practical solutions.
  • Identify repetitive, manual or spreadsheet-heavy processes that can be improved through automation.
  • Build and implement automated workflows using Power Automate or similar technologies.
  • Develop and maintain Power BI dashboards and reporting solutions.
  • Use SQL to extract, validate and analyse data from business systems.
  • Improve the quality, consistency and accessibility of information across the organisation.
  • Explore practical applications of AI and emerging technologies within existing business processes.
  • Assess potential AI use cases based on accuracy, data requirements, business value and suitability.
  • Work alongside internal IT and external technology partners on integrations, system enhancements and application changes.
  • Coordinate testing, documentation, training and implementation of new solutions.
  • Manage a prioritised programme of improvement initiatives and measure the impact of changes delivered.


What we're looking for

We're interested in people from data analytics, business improvement, automation, business systems or technology transformation backgrounds who can combine analytical thinking with hands-on delivery.

You should bring:

  • Experience delivering process improvements, reporting solutions or workflow automations.
  • Strong hands-on experience with Power BI.
  • Working knowledge of SQL and the ability to interrogate and validate business data.
  • Strong Excel skills, particularly where you have improved or replaced spreadsheet-led processes.
  • Experience using Power Automate or another workflow automation platform.
  • Strong analytical and problem-solving skills.
  • The ability to take a business problem and translate it into a practical technical solution.
  • Strong stakeholder management skills and confidence working with non-technical teams.
  • Experience managing improvements from requirements gathering through to implementation.
  • An understanding of AI tools and their potential application within a business environment, including the importance of data quality, validation and appropriate data handling.


Desirable experience

Experience in any of the following would be particularly useful:

  • Microsoft Dynamics 365 Business Central or other ERP/CRM platforms.
  • Finance, order management, stock control, retail or distribution processes.
  • Implementing AI-enabled workflows or business process automation.
  • Integrating data across multiple business systems.
  • Power Apps.
  • APIs or scripting.
  • Previous experience within technology, analytics or transformation consulting.


The opportunity

This is an opportunity to take a broad role with direct exposure to senior leadership and the ability to influence how technology is used across the organisation.

Rather than inheriting a narrow reporting remit, you'll have the scope to look across the business, identify where improvements can be made and then help deliver them.

For someone who enjoys combining data analysis, Power BI, automation, AI and business problem-solving, this offers the chance to take genuine ownership of improvement initiatives and see the impact of the solutions you deliver.

title: Lønmedarbejder
description:
AU HR Løn søger en ny kollega, som motiveres af at levere høj kvalitet, god service og korrekt løn. Du bliver en del af et dedikeret team, hvor vi arbejder med både drift og udvikling i en organisation i konstant bevægelse.

Hvad kommer du til at arbejde med?

Du får en alsidig rolle med både specialist- og supportopgaver, herunder:

  • Lønbehandling og ferieadministration
  • Refusioner, forskerbeskatning og afstemninger
  • E-indkomst og controlling via LDV-rapporter
  • Bidrag til ledelsesinformation og datakvalitet
  • Samarbejde på tværs af fagligheder og enheder
  • Overholdelse af deadlines og fokus på procesoptimering

Vi forestiller os, at du:

  • Har erfaring med løn, HR eller økonomi – og gerne kendskab til Statens Lønsystem, HR Løn og Workzone (det er ikke et krav)

  • Har blik for både detaljer og helheder – og sætter en ære i at levere kvalitet
  • Er en holdspiller, der bidrager til et godt arbejdsmiljø

Hvad tilbyder vi?

Hos os får du:

  • En hverdag med mening og faglige udfordringer
  • Et uformelt og inkluderende arbejdsmiljø med plads til humor
  • Gode muligheder for kompetenceudvikling
  • Fleksibel arbejdstid (37 timer/uge) og mulighed for hjemmearbejde
  • En arbejdsplads midt i Aarhus – tæt på både by og universitetets puls

Om os

AU HR Løn er en del af den fælles HR-organisation på Aarhus Universitet. Vi er 11 engagerede kolleger i lønteamet og ca. 70 medarbejdere i hele AU HR. Vi arbejder tæt sammen om at understøtte universitetets kerneopgaver med høj faglighed og god service.

Læs mere om os her.

Løn og ansættelsesvilkår

Du ansættes efter fællesoverenskomsten mellem Finansministeriet og Offentlige Ansattes Organisation – Det Statslige Område (OAO-S-fællesoverenskomsten) (se fællesoverenskomsten her) samt organisationsaftale for kontorfunktionærer, laboranter og It-medarbejdere (HK) (se overenskomsten her). Arbejdsstedet er Jens Chr. Skous Vej 9, 8000 Aarhus C.

Tiltrædelse er snarest muligt

Spørgsmål til stillingen

Du er meget velkommen til at kontakte:

  • Lønchef Tim Strandgaard – tsl@au.dk / 4023 8587
  • Lønmedarbejder Anita Rasmussen ar@au.dk / 8715 2298

Samtaler afholdes i uge 43.

Aarhus Universitet vil være en attraktiv og inspirerende arbejdsplads for alle og ønsker en kultur, hvor hver enkelt kan udfolde og udvikle sig. Vi ser ligestilling og diversitet som en ressource og opfordrer derfor alle interesserede til at ansøge.

The Instrumentation Lab Apprentice Program at the Tucson Proving Ground (TPG) is a two‑year, paid apprenticeship developed in partnership with Pima Community College.   • Hands‑on instrumentation experience in a world‑class proving ground environment
  • Earn while you learn: Fully paid two‑year apprenticeship with tuition support and benefits
  • Direct mentorship from experienced instrumentation and development technicians
  • Exposure to real test hardware, sensors, and data systems used in mining and construction equipment validation

  • Soldering and electronics assembly
  • Sensor installation and calibration
  • Data acquisition and measurement systems
  • Signal verification and troubleshooting
  • Technical documentation and schematic interpretation

  • Develop foundational knowledge of instrumentation systems and test environments

title: Patient Scheduler
description:
Valkyrie Clinical Trials (VCT), a Flourish Research Company, is a leading Oncology multi-site clinical research network with expertise in Oncology research. VCT approaches clinical research with a deep sense of humanity, compassion, and sincere kindness. VCT was founded by leading Clinical Oncologist, Dr. David Berz, and has multiple sites spanning California in Century City, Panaroma City, and Murrieta, and has recently expanded to Denver, Colorado.

Flourish Research is one of the industry’s most progressive and diversified clinical trial organizations, with strong capabilities across cardiology, metabolic disorders, renal, oncology, CNS, pulmonology, and vaccine research. At Flourish Research, we strive toward excellence. In clinical trials and healthcare, excellence means everyone deserves the best care, regardless of their race, color, gender identity, religion, ethnicity, physical abilities, age, sexual orientation, or veteran status. We embrace employees, customers, and patients from these underrepresented groups to help make this vision a reality. Flourish is committed to a safe work environment where all employees, customers, and patients are included, and treated with dignity and respect. The more diversity we have in our team, the more unique perspectives, and ideas we share, and the better prepared we are to serve our communities. WE SEE YOU. WE ARE YOU. WE EMBRACE YOU. WE CELEBRATE YOU!


We are actively hiring a Patient Scheduler to support our Valkyrie Clinical Trials Century City, Los Angeles, California site.

LOCATION: Onsite, Century City, CA
FLSA: Non-Exempt
HOURS: Monday to Friday, Day Shift, 40 hours per week
COMPENSATION: $22-$28 per hour (depending on experience)

PURPOSE: Serves as a first point of contact for patients and study participants, coordinating appointments and helping to ensure smooth day-to-day operations in alignment with clinic schedules. Handles a high volume of calls and scheduling requests while maintaining accuracy and patient confidentiality.

ESSENTIAL JOB FUNCTIONS:

A. Coordinate, schedule, reschedule, cancel, and follow-up on patient appointments within a site or across multiple sites.

B. Answer incoming calls and respond to patient inquiries regarding appointments, office hours, and general scheduling questions.

C. Verify patient insurance information and confirm eligibility prior to appointments.

D. Enter and update patient demographic and insurance data accurately in the EMR/practice management system.

E. Send appointment reminders via phone, text, or email.

F. Coordinate referrals and follow-up appointments with specialists as needed.

G. Manage waitlists and fill last-minute cancellations to optimize provider schedules.

H. Communicate with patient care and front desk staff as well as other clinical staff regarding scheduling conflicts, urgent add-ons, or provider availability changes.

I. Meet all deadlines established by Flourish Research SOPs, policies, and procedures.

J. Represent Flourish Research in a professional and courteous manner (verbal, written, and in appearance) during all interactions with sponsors, physicians, physicians' office personnel, participants, Flourish Research employees, Flourish Research contract personnel, as well as any other person(s) when carrying out task and responsibilities.

K. Maintain confidentiality of information and issues relating to patients, study participants, protocol, and/or contracted entities.

L. Comply with HIPAA, GCP, and clinic policies.

M. Assist with other front-office, administrative, and operational duties as needed, including cross-functional coverage of front desk duties as required.

N. Additional duties as assigned or required by management.

PHYSICAL REQUIREMENTS AND/OR ENVIRONMENTAL FACTORS:

A. Work is normally performed in a typical interior/office work environment.

B. Occasional local travel may be required.

C. Daily computer use.

D. Ability to properly lift 10 pounds and occasionally more than 10 pounds.

E. Frequent contact with patients, physicians, and other center staff.

F. Ability to work in an environment which at times may be stressful, including frequent interactions with others, interruptions, multiple calls and inquiries, and potentially emotional situations.

G. Manual dexterity to operate a computer, telephone, copier, fax, and other such office equipment as necessary.

H. Occasional overtime work as needed.

Requirements

MINIMUM REQUIREMENTS:

Education: High school diploma or equivalent required; some college coursework preferred.

Experience: 1+ years of experience in medical scheduling, front-office healthcare administration, or a related customer service role. Experience working in a multi-provider or high-volume clinic preferred.

Knowledge and Skills:

A. Familiarity with electronic medical records (EMR) and practice management software strongly preferred.

B. Strong understanding of medical terminology and insurance verification processes preferred.

C. Prior experience with insurance authorizations and referrals.

D. Excellent verbal and written communication skills. Able to communicate clearly, professionally, and effectively in person, in writing, or by phone.

E. Ability to collaborate and align with both internal and external stakeholders.

F. Excellent customer service skills for both inter and intra department.

G. Demonstrates professionalism, confidentiality, and sound decision-making.

H. Ability to manage high volume calls, messages, call routing, and follow-up communications.

I. Ability to maintain records and documentation in an accurate and timely manner.

J. Ability to communicate effectively with patients to provide clear and thorough instructions, answer questions, and complete required processes.

K. Excellent computer skills to include Office365 products.

L. Ability to learn and demonstrate compliance with company policies and procedures.

M. Strong organizational skills and ability to multitask in a fast-paced environment

N. Ability to work both independently and in a team environment.

O. Consistently demonstrate Flourish Research’s core values.

Benefits

Health, dental, and vision insurance plans, 401(k) with a 100% employer match on the first 4% of employee contributions, tuition reimbursement, parental leave, employee referral program, employee assistance program, life insurance, disability insurance, and a generous PTO plan covering vacation, sick, personal days and 8 paid holidays.

Flourish Research is an equal employment opportunity employer. Employment decisions are based on merit and business needs, and not on race, color, sex, (including pregnancy and gender identity), citizenship status, national origin, ancestry, gender, sexual orientation, age, religion, creed, physical or mental disability, genetic information, marital status, veteran status, political affiliation, or any other factor protected by law. Flourish Research complies with the law regarding reasonable accommodation for handicapped and disabled employees.

description:

Key Details: Applicants for this position have the flexibility to work remotely from their home anywhere within the state of Michigan. This role provides telephonic support to foster care children. The work schedule is Monday - Friday, 8am - 4:30pm.

  • Evaluates the needs of the member, barriers to care, the resources available, and recommends and facilitates the plan for the best outcome
  • Develops or contributes to the development of a personalized care plan/service ongoing care plans/service plans and works to identify providers, specialists, and/or community resources needed for care
  • Provides psychosocial and resource support to members/caregivers, and care managers to access local resources or services such as: employment, education, housing, food, participant direction, independent living, justice, foster care) based on service assessment and plans
  • Coordinates as appropriate between the member and/or family/caregivers and the care provider team to ensure identified care or services are accessible to members in a timely manner
  • May monitor progress towards care plans/service plans goals and/or member status or change in condition, and collaborates with healthcare providers for care plan/service plan revision or address identified member needs, refer to care management for further evaluation as appropriate
  • Collects, documents, and maintains all member information and care management activities to ensure compliance with current state, federal, and third-party payer regulators
  • May perform on-site visits to assess member’s needs and collaborate with providers or resources, as appropriate
  • May provide education to care manager and/or members and their families/caregivers on procedures, healthcare provider instructions, care options, referrals, and healthcare benefits

The Supply Chain Specialist is responsible for planning, coordinating, and optimizing the flow of purchased and manufactured products through the internal distribution network to ensure timely, cost-effective, and accurate delivery to customers. This role works closely with sales, services, manufacturing, shipping & receiving, and logistics to maintain inventory availability and support business objectives. They support material availability, inventory accuracy, and continuous improvement initiatives in alignment with company safety, quality, and operational standards.

Key Responsibilities:

1. Maintain appropriate and accurate physical and electronic/ERP inventory levels of sellable goods to prevent sales or service disruptions.
2. Monitor inventory requirements and initiate replenishment activities.
3. Responsible for creation and life cycle management of purchase orders for goods and services in alignment with demand, planning signals, and company procedures.
4. Create and monitor intercompany transfer orders between distribution yard and remote sales locations.
5. Support planning activities for site assembly and other value-added operations.
6. Create, maintain, and execute cycle count schedules and ABC classifications as directed.

11. Ensure material identification, labeling, and storage standards are maintained to support accuracy and traceability.

**_Job Title: Lead Systems Engineer_**

**_Job Code: 45046_**

**_Job Location: Salt Lake City, Utah_**

**_Job Schedule: 9/80: Employees work 9 out of every 14 days- totaling 80 hours worked- and have every other Friday off_**

**Job Description**

The Lead Systems Engineer will serve as the primary engineering interface for Customer Platforms supporting the sustainment of mission-critical communications capabilities.

This role leads complex, cross-functional engineering efforts spanning operational support, flight test, software releases, system integration, verification, configuration management, and obsolescence management. The Lead Systems Engineer will work directly with Customers, program leadership, internal engineering teams, suppliers, and subcontractors to resolve technical issues, influence engineering priorities, and ensure delivered capabilities meet mission, contractual, and operational requirements.

The ideal candidate is a recognized systems engineering subject-matter expert with strong customer engagement skills, experience supporting fielded systems, and the ability to independently lead initiatives of substantial importance to the program.

**Essential Functions**

- Serve as the primary engineering point of contact for assigned Customer Platforms
- Attend and lead engineering participation in recurring Technical Interchange Meetings (TIMs), customer meetings, program reviews, and technical briefings.
- Lead the investigation, prioritization, coordination, and resolution of Customer-reported operational issues, ensuring timely technical communication and appropriate escalation.
- Coordinate cross-functional engineering teams to assess impacts, establish corrective actions, manage technical risks, and verify resolution of fielded-system issues.
- Plan and support flight test, integration, verification, qualification, and operational test events at customer locations.
- Lead systems engineering support for new software releases, including requirements assessment, configuration and interface impact analysis, release readiness, deployment coordination, and post-release issue resolution.
- Lead DMSMS and obsolescence efforts for supported systems, coordinating with suppliers, program management, logistics, and design engineering to develop technically sound and cost-effective mitigation plans.
- Maintain technical awareness of Customer Platform configurations, operational environments, interfaces, open issues, risks, and planned upgrades.
- Develop and maintain systems engineering artifacts, including requirements, interface control documents, technical assessments, test plans, verification cross-reference matrices, release documentation, and risk registers.
- Provide technical leadership across engineering disciplines, guiding work priorities and reviewing technical products to ensure quality, completeness, and compliance with program processes.
- Identify and implement improvements to sustainment engineering processes, issue-management workflows, release practices, and customer communication methods that improve program and operational outcomes.
- Prepare and present technical recommendations, status, risks, and resolution plans to customers, program leadership, engineering leadership, and senior stakeholders.
- Support proposal development, customer RFIs/RFPs, technical demonstrations, and new business pursuits as needed.
- Ability to obtain and maintain an active U.S. Government DoD Top Secret security clearance.

**Qualifications**

- Bachelor’s degree in Systems Engineering, Electrical Engineering, Computer Engineering, Computer Science, or a related technical discipline, with a minimum of 9 years of prior relevant experience; or a graduate degree with a minimum of 7 years of prior related experience.
- In lieu of a degree, a minimum of 13 years of prior related experience.

**Preferred Additional Skills**

- Demonstrated experience leading complex systems engineering, integration, verification, sustainment, or lifecycle-support efforts with minimal oversight.
- Experience serving as a technical interface with military customers, platform operators, or operational users.
- Experience supporting airborne, space, ground, tactical, satellite, or line-of-sight communications systems.
- Experience with fielded-system sustainment, operational issue resolution, software release management, DMSMS, and configuration management.
- Experience planning or supporting flight test, system integration, verification, qualification, or customer-site test events.
- Strong knowledge of requirements management, interface management, risk management, technical planning, and verification and validation.
- Demonstrated ability to lead and influence cross-functional teams, customers, suppliers, and subcontractors without formal management authority.
- Experience with tools such as DOORS or similar requirements-management tools, Microsoft Word, Excel, PowerPoint, Project, and Visio.

description:
PageWide Industrial Strategic Sourcing Lead

Description -

We are seeking a Strategic Sourcing & Contract Manufacturing Lead to define and advance the organization’s approach to managing contract manufacturers and critical suppliers. This role establishes supplier governance and commercial standards, leads complex sourcing and negotiation strategies, and provides senior oversight for supplier performance, operational readiness, risk, and continuous improvement.

Serving as a functional leader and advisor, the position guides supplier relationship owners and cross-functional partners in making consistent, well-informed decisions that balance business requirements, supply continuity, and long-term supplier capability.

The ideal candidate brings extensive strategic sourcing and contract manufacturing experience, strong commercial judgment, and the ability to influence senior stakeholders and improve organizational capability without relying on direct authority.



Responsibilities

Contract Manufacturing and Supplier Performance

Define and lead the management model for contract manufacturers and critical suppliers, including governance, performance expectations, review cadence, escalation protocols, and continuous improvement priorities.

Establish expectations for cost, quality, delivery, inventory, capacity, responsiveness, compliance, operational readiness, and business continuity.

Guide supplier relationship owners in resolving complex commercial, operational, quality, and supply continuity issues.

Lead supplier performance reviews and long-term improvement plans that deliver measurable business results.

Partner with Operations, Engineering, Quality, Finance, and Program Management to align supplier capabilities and deliverables with business requirements.

Provide senior recommendations on supplier selection, transitions, capacity, investments, production readiness, and risk acceptance.

Sourcing, Contracts, and Commercial Governance

Develop and maintain sourcing and supplier-management standards, tools, and scorecards covering segmentation, strategy, performance reviews, corrective actions, contract alignment, financial health, escalation, and risk mitigation.

Lead negotiation strategies for complex or high-risk engagements, including objectives, leverage, target outcomes, concessions, approvals, walk-away positions, and commercial risk tradeoffs.

Partner with HP Sourcing and Legal stakeholders to strengthen contract standards, commercial guardrails, and review governance.

Identify systemic gaps and lead improvements that strengthen accountability, consistency, and executive decision-making.

Functional Leadership and Organizational Capability

Provide functional leadership and mentoring to team members managing suppliers, commodities, and contract manufacturing partners.

Advise team members and leaders on supplier strategy, negotiations, executive communications, escalations, and cross-functional alignment.

Review supplier strategies and performance assessments before major engagements or decisions.

Develop reusable tools, templates, playbooks, and best practices that improve supplier-management capability across the organization.


Education and Experience

Bachelor's degree in Supply Chain Management, Engineering, Business, Finance, Operations Management, or a related discipline; advanced degree preferred.

Typically 12+ years of progressively responsible experience in strategic sourcing, supplier management, procurement, supply chain, contract manufacturing, or related fields.

Demonstrated record of leading complex supplier strategies, contract manufacturing governance, supplier performance, negotiations, and commercial decisions while influencing senior stakeholders and cross-functional teams.

Strong understanding of contract manufacturing business models, supplier relationship management, commercial agreements, and manufacturing operations.

Exceptional communication, coaching, negotiation, influence, and stakeholder management skills.


Preferred Qualifications

Experience within industrial equipment, manufacturing, printing, or technology industries.

Experience leading global suppliers and multinational sourcing projects.

Professional certifications such as CPSM, CPM, CSCP, or equivalent.

title: Pastoral Care Officer (Primary School – Student Well-being)
description:
Job Details

  • Working Hours: Mondays to Fridays, 7:15 AM – 2:45 PM (Inclusive of a 1-hour lunch break).Additional hours may occasionally be required to support students, paid at an hourly rate.Service is typically not required on Saturdays, Sundays, gazetted public holidays, and school holidays.
  • Location: Tao Nan School – 49 Marine Crescent, Singapore 449761 (Managed by the Singapore Hokkien Huay Kuan).

Job Description & Core Responsibilities

We are looking for an empathetic, patient, and highly structured individual to step into the role of a Pastoral Care Officer. Your main objective is to provide critical emotional, social, and behavioral guidance to primary school students, serving as a trusted pillar within the school's ecosystem.

1. Student Emotional & Behavioral Support

  • First Line of Support: Provide specialized one-on-one pastoral guidance for primary school students who are feeling anxious, distressed, withdrawn, or emotionally overwhelmed.
  • Constructive Management: Apply modern restorative practices, active listening, and proven de-escalation strategies to handle sensitive playground or classroom incidents constructively.
  • Safe Environment: Build authentic, trusting relationships with students while establishing a safe, confidential space for them to process their concerns.

2. Case Management & Well-being Monitoring

  • Risk Identification: Actively identify and closely monitor students who may be vulnerable or at-risk due to mental health, social integration, or complex family dynamics.
  • Coordinated Support: Conduct regular check-ins and track changes in student behavior, attendance, and general wellness. Collaborate seamlessly with Year Heads (YH), School Counselors, and the Discipline Mistress.
  • Record Keeping: Keep immaculate, confidential documentation of student progress, behavioral changes, and early intervention notes.

3. Crisis Intervention & Safeguarding

  • Rapid Response: Act immediately during live student meltdowns, emotional breakdowns, peer conflicts, or aggressive behavioral issues.
  • Stabilization: Focus on de-escalating heightened scenarios safely, prioritizing the physical and psychological safety of all parties involved.

4. Wellness Programming & Stakeholder Engagement

  • Preventive Initiatives: Support, plan, and conduct proactive Social-Emotional Learning (SEL) activities and school-wide peer support programs.
  • Family Communication: Coordinate and communicate with parents or guardians with high sensitivity regarding student well-being and updates.
  • External Networking: Partner with external community resources, social services, and mental health professionals when specialized care escalations are required.

Job Requirements

  • Minimum Qualification: At least a Diploma in Counselling, Psychology, Social Work, Education, or a related behavioral science discipline.
  • Proven Track Record: Minimum of 2 years of experience in primary school student well-being, pastoral care, or behavioral support; OR 2 years of direct exposure to counseling and mentoring students aged 7 to 12 with social-emotional needs.
  • Core Competencies:Superb active listening and communication skills tailored to primary-school-aged children.Ability to remain fully calm, patient, and composed during high-stress student meltdowns.Basic competence in student conflict resolution and positive behavior reinforcement models.
  • Ethical Standard: High level of integrity, with an ironclad commitment to maintaining student confidentiality and executing sound judicial boundaries. Selected personnel must sign an official Undertaking to Safeguard Official Information form.
