title: Principal Chemist
description:
Imagine how your ideas and expertise can change a patient’s life. Our Global Operations & Quality team plays a central part in ensuring our products are delivered to patients with cardiovascular disease. You’ll partner cross-functionally with manufacturing operations and sales teams, delivering thoughtful solutions to complex challenges all while developing your knowledge of the medical device industry. Whether your work includes strategic inventory planning, labeling, warehouse management, material handling, or any of our other supply chain opportunities, you will be making a meaningful contribution to our team and to patients all over the world.


This is an opportunity to join a state-of-the-art medical device chemical characterization laboratory and center of excellence for analytical chemistry and unknowns analysis. The Principal Chemist will specialize in mass spectrometry-based structural elucidation of extractables and leachables and the development, validation, optimization, and troubleshooting of analytical methods using liquid chromatography mass spectrometer (LC-MS and gas chromatography mass spectrometer (GC-MS), with inductively coupled mass spectrometer (ICP-MS) and related technologies supporting broader chemical characterization and complex investigations.


How you’ll make an impact:

  • Support the test method development, validation, and testing on Extractables and Leachables using high performance liquid chromatography mass spectrometer (HPLC-MS), GC-MS, and ICP-MS.
  • Perform mass spec structural elucidation of extractables and leachables.
  • Support routine analysis of leachables and extractables and EO/ECH residual on medical device.
  • Assist in test method development and validation for a variety of cleaning validations using GC-MS, GC-MS/HS, HPLC-MS, HPLC-DAD, ICP-MS, TOC, FT-IR, UV, etc.
  • Own technical direction for complex laboratory methods, instrumentation platforms, and investigation approaches across multiple workstreams. Provide technical oversight for complex testing, data review, and qualification strategies for new or modified devices and/or processes.
  • Provide technical authority for root cause analysis of product/sample failures and Out-of-Specifications (OOS), incidents, deviations and their significance, non-conformances, and CAPA; review technical conclusions, resolve escalated issues, and determine appropriate corrective and preventive actions.
  • Establish technical expectations and execute development, modification, verification, validation, transfer, and lifecycle management of methods, lab-specific protocols, and reports in collaboration with intra- and inter-departmental teams.
  • Define technical strategy for equipment qualifications and software validation activities for complex analytical systems and ensure alignment to laboratory and quality requirements.
  • Establish expectations and perform interpretation of data and analysis of results, including statements of conformity or opinions and interpretations, trend analysis, and qualification strategies for new or modified devices and/or processes.
  • Lead standardization of laboratory practices, technical decision-making, and review expectations across assigned methods, platforms, or programs.
  • Lead complex process improvement projects (e.g., BEST, 6S, Lean), update procedures/forms, support safety and quality initiatives, and implement sustainable changes with management approval.
  • Mentor and technically guide lower-level or new employees; report, review and authorize results; assess work techniques and provide feedback on procedures, methods, and technical rigor.

What you’ll need (Required):

  • Bachelor's Degree in Chemistry or equivalent with 8 years of previous related experience with unknowns analysis using mass spectrometry techniques and/or structural elucidation; OR
  • Master's Degree in Chemistry or equivalent with 6 years of previous related experience with unknowns analysis using mass spectrometry techniques and/or structural elucidation; OR
  • Ph.D. or equivalent in Chemistry or equivalent with 4 years of previous related experience with unknowns analysis using mass spectrometry techniques and/or structural elucidation.
  • On‑site presence required to collaborate cross‑functionally and support manufacturing operations.
  • Travel requirement up to 25%.

What else we look for (Preferred):

  • Extensive knowledge and understanding of chemical principles, theories and concepts.
  • Extensive knowledge of laboratory equipment (e.g., gas Chromatography, high performance liquid chromatography, total organic carbon, fourier transform infrared spectroscopy, atomic absorption).
  • Full knowledge in the review, evaluation, interpretation, and implementation of internal and external guidance's (e.g., ISO, GLP/GMP/QSIT).
  • Knowledge of Good Manufacturing and Good Documentation Practices supporting a medical device environment.
  • Proven successful project management skills.
  • Proven expertise in MS Office; Analytical Equipment System (e.g., ChemStation, MassHunter).
  • Excellent communication skills and interpersonal relationship skills including negotiating and relationship management skills with ability to drive achievement of objectives.

title: Analyst, IT Configuration Management Database
description:
The Analyst – IT Configuration Management Database (CMDB) supports the day-to-day maintenance, data quality, and governance of the enterprise CMDB.


The role is responsible for ensuring Configuration Items (CIs), attributes, ownership information, lifecycle status, and relationships are accurate, complete, and maintained in accordance with established Configuration Management standards and ITSM practices.


The Analyst works with Application, Infrastructure, and other technology teams to maintain reliable configuration data and support operational and service management processes.


Key Responsibilities

  • CMDB Administration & Data Quality
    • Create, update, validate, and maintain Configuration Items and related attributes in the CMDB.
    • Support CI onboarding, modification, ownership changes, lifecycle updates, and decommissioning.
    • Review CMDB data for completeness, accuracy, duplicates, stale records, and missing information.
    • Assist with CI certification, reconciliation, and data-quality remediation activities.
    • Maintain and validate relationships between applications, infrastructure, cloud resources, and business services.
    • Work with CI owners and technical teams to resolve data-quality issues.
    • Ensure CMDB records are updated following approved infrastructure or application changes.
  • Discovery, Reporting & ITSM Support
    • Support automated discovery, integrations, imports, and reconciliation activities used to maintain CMDB data.
    • Review discovery and integration exceptions and coordinate remediation with appropriate teams.
    • Prepare basic CMDB reports, dashboards, and data-quality metrics.
    • Support related ITSM processes such as Incident, Problem, Change, and Asset Management by providing accurate CI information.
    • Assist with audit, governance, and compliance requests related to CMDB data.
    • Maintain CMDB procedures, work instructions, and supporting documentation.
    • Identify opportunities to improve data quality, process consistency, and automation.

Required Qualifications

  • Bachelor’s degree in information technology, Computer Science, Information Systems, or a related field, or equivalent relevant experience.
  • 2–3 years of experience in IT Service Management, Configuration Management, IT Operations, IT Asset Management, or a related technology function.
  • Experience working with ServiceNow CMDB or a comparable ITSM/CMDB platform.
  • Basic understanding of Configuration Items, CI relationships, lifecycle management, and CMDB data-quality principles.
  • General knowledge of enterprise technologies, including applications, servers, networks, databases, and cloud environments.
  • Strong attention to detail, analytical ability, and problem-solving skills.
  • Good written and verbal communication skills.

title: Structural Systems Engineer
description:
## **Job Details**

New ideas are all around us, but only a few will change the world. That’s our focus at JPL. We ask the biggest questions, then search the universe for answers—literally. We build upon ideas that have guided generations, then share our discoveries to inspire generations to come. Your mission—your opportunity—is to seek out the answers that bring us one step closer. If you’re driven to discover, create, and inspire something that lasts a lifetime and beyond, you’re ready for JPL.

Located in Pasadena, California, JPL has a campus-like environment situated on 177 acres in the foothills of the San Gabriel Mountains and offers a work environment unlike any other: we inspire passion, foster innovation, build collaboration, and reward excellence.

This unique opportunity is part of the **Mechanical and Control Systems Division (35)**, which creates advanced mechanical, robotics, thermal, propulsion, onboard GNC, and electronic packaging systems. Division 35 develops hardware and systems from early architecture through design, fabrication, subsystem, and system-level integration and test.

You will be working as a _**Structural Systems Engineer**_ within the **Mechanical Engineering, Integration, and Test Section**, which leads the design, analysis, development, integration, and test of flight mechanical and robotic systems for spacecraft, payloads, and ground-based systems. In this role, you will:

- Perform structural design and analysis to ensure the structural integrity of subsystem and system-level hardware and the associated support structures.
- Perform structural analysis utilizing classical solutions and finite element analysis (FEA) method for flight projects and/or technology tasks and/or proposal developments.
- Perform detailed stress/structural analysis, dynamic analysis, and pre-test analysis.
- Build finite element models from scratch, using hand calculations when appropriate, to determine critical areas in structure and determine efficient and adequate approaches for analysis independently.

- Contribute to the design process of mechanical assemblies from engineering requirements to engineering drawings including suggestions and feedback on areas of concern based on analysis, mechanical intuition, and engineering judgement.

- Support and present analysis results at team, line management, and technical reviews.
- Support and conduct static and dynamic tests and develop test reports.
- Perform tasks under the direction of the group supervisor, project management, and project technical leads, work independently and within a team environment, and collaborate on tasks that span a spectrum of disciplines.

**Required Skills:**

- Bachelor’s degree in Mechanical Engineering or related technical discipline with a minimum of 3 years of related experience; or a Master’s degree with a minimum of 1 year related experience or PhD in similar disciplines.

- Experience and knowledge in structural engineering, analysis, and verification of flight structures (spacecraft or instruments), composite structures, mechanisms, and/or opto-mechanical assemblies.
- Experience in MSC.Nastran, NX-Nastran, FEMAP, Abaqus, MSC.ADAMS or LS-DYNA.
- General knowledge of industry and/or academic practices and standards related to structural mechanics, finite element analysis, and structural verification testing.

**Desired Skills:**

- Experience in completing structural analysis of complex and unique flight mechanical systems and detailed analysis of its components.
- Ability to present structural margins & analyses to project management and provide design recommendations.
- Ability to develop and conduct structural verification test programs for space flight hardware.
- Ability to troubleshoot mechanical, mechanism, and/or structural anomalies and failures.
- Ability to develop innovative design solutions to meet design requirements and resolve technical challenges.
- Knowledge of Standards for Geometric Dimensioning and Tolerancing (GD&T) per American Society of Mechanical Engineers (ASME) Y14.5.
- Excellent verbal and written communication skills.
- Excellent collaboration skills and ability to work across subject areas and organizations.

This includes a variety of health, dental, vision, wellbeing, and retirement plans, paid time off, learning, rideshare, childcare, flexible schedule, parental leave and many more. title: Finishing Operator
description:
About Us

Amarr, a part of ASSA ABLOY, the global leaders in opening solutions, is a performance driven manufacturing organization committed to safety, quality, and operational excellence. As an industry leader, we empower our teams to innovate, continuously improve, and deliver world class solutions to our customers.

The Finishing Operator primarily supports powder coating operations by preparing materials, selecting the appropriate finish, loading components onto finishing systems, applying coatings, conducting quality inspections, and packaging or moving finished products to designated locations.

Shift: Monday - Thursday; 7am - 5:30pm

Key Responsibilities

  • Review and interpret cut sheets, work orders, and manufacturing specifications to determine required colors, finishes, and processing requirements.
  • Obtain, identify, and stage materials and components for finishing operations.
  • Inspect incoming components for defects, cleanliness, and readiness for finishing.
  • Prepare components for finishing through cleaning, masking, plugging, grinding, or other required preparation processes.
  • Load and hang components onto racks, hooks, or gantry systems to ensure proper coating coverage and efficient processing.
  • Set up and operate powder coating and other finishing equipment according to established procedures.
  • Perform color changes and finish changeover procedures while maintaining contamination control and quality standards.
  • Monitor coating application processes to ensure proper coverage, appearance, and finish quality.
  • Apply powder coat and other approved finishing materials according to specifications.
  • Verify coating thickness, finish appearance, gloss, and color match using approved quality inspection methods and tools.
  • Conduct in-process and final quality inspections to ensure finished products meet customer and engineering requirements.
  • Identify, segregate, and report non-conforming materials, finishes, or products.
  • Load and unload materials from curing ovens and finishing systems using approved handling procedures.
  • Move finished products to designated staging, storage, assembly, or shipping locations.
  • Maintain accurate production, quality, and material documentation as required.
  • Troubleshoot minor equipment and process issues and communicate concerns to supervision.
  • Perform routine cleaning and housekeeping activities to maintain equipment and work areas.
  • Follow all safety procedures related to powder coating materials, compressed air systems, chemicals, ovens, material handling equipment, and personal protective equipment.
  • Support continuous improvement initiatives focused on safety, quality, delivery, and productivity.
  • All other duties and special projects assigned.

Position Requirements

  • High school diploma or GED preferred.
  • Ability to read and interpret cut sheets, work instructions, and manufacturing specifications.
  • Ability to safely operate hand tools, powered tools, and assembly equipment.
  • Basic understanding of measurements and dimensional requirements.
  • Ability to use measuring devices such as tape measures and other inspection tools.
  • Basic computer skills for production reporting and documentation.
  • Strong attention to detail and commitment to quality.
  • Ability to work effectively both independently and as part of a team.

Preferred Qualifications

  • Experience with powder coating, industrial finishing, or paint application processes.
  • Experience performing color changeovers and finish changeover procedures.
  • Experience using coating thickness gauges and other quality inspection equipment.
  • Experience working around curing ovens, conveyors, and finishing systems.
  • Experience with lean manufacturing and 5S principles.
  • Forklift or material handling equipment experience.

Other Job Responsibilities and Physical Requirements

  • Ability to lift up to 45 lbs. unassisted with or without reasonable accommodation.
  • Ability to lift, carry, push, and/or pull materials weighing more than 45 lbs. using team lifting procedures.
  • Ability to stand and/or walk for extended periods (8–12 hours per shift).
  • Ability to safely move throughout the manufacturing floor.
  • Ability to bend, kneel, crouch, climb stairs and/or ladders as required for job tasks.
  • Ability to use hands, wrists, and fingers for handling materials, writing, and computer work.
  • Frequent use of computers, keyboards, tablets, scanners, or handheld devices.
  • Ability to work in a loud, fast-paced industrial environment.
  • Ability to work in hot and cold environmental conditions.

Benefits include Medical/Dental/Vision, Paid Time Off, and a 401k plan (with an automatic 3% company contribution, regardless of your contribution) among others.

Our goal is to be a world-leading company that attracts diverse talent, where all team members feel safe being their true selves and are able to thrive in a work environment that promotes change, innovation, and provides equal access and opportunity.

All qualified applicants will receive consideration for employment without regard to race, color, religion, sex, sexual orientation, gender identity, national origin, disability, or status as a protected veteran. Amarr is an E-Verify participant.

  • Playwright

  • Experience developing and maintaining automated testing frameworks.
  • Experience with CI/CD pipelines, including: Jenkins GitLab CI

title: Software Engineer
description:
The Software Engineer (Python / PySpark / AI) is responsible for designing, developing, and maintaining production-grade Python applications and services, with a strong emphasis on core software engineering fundamentals, clean design, and solid database work.

The role includes writing and tuning PySpark jobs for large-scale data
processing, and building AI-enabled capabilities such as LLM-backed services, retrieval pipelines, and ML feature/inference workflows. Depth in Python, databases, and engineering craftsmanship remains the primary focus. AI work is treated as software engineering: the engineer is expected to integrate models into dependable systems with proper evaluation, observability, and cost controls, rather than to conduct original model research. Exposure to broader data engineering practices such as orchestration, lakehouse formats, and pipeline design is valuable.

The engineer collaborates closely with other developers, architects, data scientists, and project managers to translate business requirements into working software.
  • Design, develop, and maintain scalable, high-quality applications and services in Python.
  • Write clean, maintainable, well-tested, and efficient code following established design principles and team standards.
  • Develop and optimize PySpark jobs for batch and large-volume data processing workloads.
  • Build AI-enabled features: integrate LLM and ML APIs or self-hosted models into backend services, including prompt design, structured output handling, tool/function calling, and graceful fallback behavior.
  • Implement retrieval-augmented generation (RAG) components: chunking and embedding pipelines, vector search, retrieval quality tuning, and grounding/citation handling.
  • Build data preparation and feature pipelines that feed model training, fine-tuning, and inference, using Spark where scale requires it.
  • Operationalize AI workloads: batch and real-time inference paths, caching, token and cost monitoring, latency budgets, rate limiting, and retry semantics.
  • Contribute to AI evaluation and quality: build regression test sets, offline evaluation harnesses, and guardrails for accuracy, hallucination, safety, and PII handling.
  • Model, query, and tune relational data: write efficient SQL, design schemas, and reason about indexes, joins, and query plans.
  • Build and consume REST APIs and integrations with backend, data, and AI services.
  • Troubleshoot and debug production issues, including performance bottlenecks, memory issues, data correctness problems, and non-deterministic model behavior.
  • Profile and optimize applications, Spark jobs, and AI inference paths for runtime, resource usage, and cost.
  • Use AI-assisted development tools responsibly to improve delivery speed while maintaining code quality, security, and review standards.
  • Participate in code reviews, design discussions, and technical documentation.
  • Work independently and as part of a team to deliver projects on time.
  • Bachelor's degree in Computer Science or a related field.
  • 3-5 years of experience building applications in Python.
  • Strong command of core Python: data structures, OOP, error handling, iterators/generators, concurrency basics, packaging, and virtual environments.
  • Solid computer science fundamentals: data structures, algorithms, complexity analysis, and debugging methodology.
  • Strong SQL skills and hands-on experience with at least one relational database (PostgreSQL, MySQL, Oracle, or SQL Server).
  • Working knowledge of PySpark or a strong willingness to develop it on the job, including DataFrame APIs and basic understanding of distributed execution.
  • Practical exposure to AI/ML in software: consuming LLM or ML model APIs, working with embeddings, or integrating a model into an application, with an understanding of prompt behavior, context limits, and non-determinism.
  • Experience with automated testing (pytest or equivalent) and writing testable code.
  • Experience with Git or other version control systems.
  • Excellent problem-solving and analytical skills.
  • Ability to work independently and as part of a team.
  • Strong communication skills.
  • Hands-on experience with LLM application frameworks and tooling (LangChain, LlamaIndex, Semantic Kernel, or equivalent) and agentic/tool-calling patterns.
  • Experience with vector databases or vector search (pgvector, OpenSearch, FAISS, Pinecone, Milvus, or similar).
  • Experience with the Python ML/data stack (pandas, NumPy, scikit-learn) and familiarity with PyTorch or TensorFlow.
  • Exposure to MLOps and LLMOps practices: model/prompt versioning, experiment tracking (MLflow or similar), model registries, deployment, drift monitoring, and AI observability/tracing.
  • Familiarity with fine-tuning or parameter-efficient tuning approaches, and knowing when retrieval or prompting is the better trade-off.
  • Awareness of responsible AI concerns: data privacy, PII redaction, bias, prompt injection, and secure handling of model inputs and outputs.
  • Experience tuning Spark jobs: partitioning, shuffles, joins, caching, and reading execution plans.
  • Familiarity with data engineering practices such as ETL/ELT pipeline design, incremental loads, and data quality checks.
  • Exposure to lakehouse table formats (Delta Lake, Iceberg, Hudi) or columnar formats (Parquet, ORC).
  • Experience with workflow orchestration tools (Airflow, Dagster, or similar).
  • Working knowledge of cloud platforms (AWS, Azure, or GCP), managed Spark offerings (EMR, Databricks, Glue), and managed AI services (Amazon Bedrock/SageMaker, Azure OpenAI, or Vertex AI).
  • Experience with containers and CI/CD (Docker, Kubernetes, GitLab CI, or Jenkins).
  • Familiarity with NoSQL or streaming systems (Kafka, DynamoDB, MongoDB).
  • Familiarity with Agile development methodologies is a plus.

title: Senior konsult inom vattenmiljö eller dagvatten
description:
Senior konsult inom vattenmiljö eller dagvatten

Vill du leda kvalificerade vattenprojekt och samtidigt få stor möjlighet att påverka din roll och vår fortsatta utveckling? Hagströms Vattenvård & Miljörätt söker en senior konsult inom vattenmiljö eller dagvatten.

Om oss

Hagströms Vattenvård & Miljörätt AB är ett mindre miljökonsultbolag med stor kunskap och erfarenhet av komplexa uppdrag inom vatten och miljö. Företaget grundades 2019 och vi tar oss an uppdrag i hela Sverige. Vi utreder, projekterar och arbetsleder bland annat miljöanpassningar av dammar (fiskvägar, dammutrivningar) och vägtrummor, restaurering av vattendrag och våtmarker. Vi jobbar även med dagvattenprojekt. Vi hjälper också våra uppdragsgivare i tillståndsprocesser hos mark- och miljödomstolen.

Uppdragsgivare är bland andra vattenkraftsbolag, skogsbolag, Trafikverket, länsstyrelser, kommuner, vattenvårdsförbund och fiskevårdsområdesföreningar.

Du blir en del av ett litet, engagerat och prestigelöst team med tillväxtambitioner. Arbetet bedrivs projektbaserat och du har stor flexibilitet och goda möjligheter att forma din roll.

Om rollen

Som senior konsult och uppdragsledare driver du projekt med varierande innehåll, omfattning och komplexitet. Du arbetar självständigt eller tillsammans med kollegor, beroende på uppdragets behov. Du är trygg i din roll, leder arbetet framåt och löser de problem som uppstår och stöttar där det behövs. Rollen kombinerar tekniskt arbete med en nära dialog med våra kunder, kvalitetssäkring och utveckling av våra arbetssätt. I din roll ingår bland annat att

· leda och genomföra uppdrag från planering till leverans

· utreda, projektera och ta fram bygghandlingar

· genomföra hydrauliska och hydrologiska beräkningar

· ta fram tekniska beskrivningar, rapporter

· medverka vid framtagande av diverse tillståndshandlingar och vid behov delta på samrådsmöten och domstolsförhandlingar

· bygga förtroendefulla relationer med uppdragsgivare och samarbetspartner

· bidra med granskning, kvalitetssäkring och kunskapsdelning i teamet

· medverka i anbudsarbete och affärsutveckling.

Beroende på din erfarenhet och inriktning kan du få en viktig roll i att utveckla vårt erbjudande och bygga upp ett verksamhetsområde inom exempelvis vattenbyggnad eller dagvatten.

Tjänsten är en tillsvidareanställning som inleds med sex månaders provanställning. Tillträde snarast eller enligt överenskommelse.

Vi söker dig som

Du är ansvarstagande, samarbetsinriktad och van att driva uppdrag framåt. Du är resultatorienterad med ett strukturerat arbetssätt med stort fokus på kvalitet och trivs med att dela kunskap, erfarenheter och idéer.

· har minst 5 -10 års relevant yrkeserfarenhet

· har erfarenhet av att självständigt leda och ansvara för projekt

· har erfarenhet av utredning, projektering och framtagande av bygghandlingar för exempelvis fiskpassager eller andra vattenvårdsåtgärder alternativt dagvattenlösningar

· mycket god förmåga att uttrycka dig på svenska i tal och skrift

· har B-körkort och möjlighet att resa och tillfälligt arbeta på annan ort när uppdragen kräver det.

Du behöver vara civilingenjör inom miljö- och vattenteknik, väg och vatten eller inneha annan relevant teknisk/naturvetenskaplig akademisk utbildning.

Meriterande erfarenheter

Det är meriterande om du har erfarenhet av något eller flera av följande områden:

· hydrauliska beräkningar och modellering

· CAD eller SketchUp i 2D och 3D

· HEC-RAS eller andra motsvarande programvaror

· GIS

· StormTac

· Projektering/bygghandling fiskvägar

· Projektering/bygghandling vägtrummor med broklassning enligt kravdokumnet TRV

· Utredning och/eller projektering av dagvattenlösningar

· Översvämningskartering och skyfallsutredningar

· Dammbrotts- och konsekvensutredningar

· NAP-prövningar

· Recipientutredningar

· AMA

· Arbets- eller byggledning vid genomförandefasen

· Brett kontaktnät

Det här erbjuder vi

· varierade och kvalificerade uppdrag med tydlig miljönytta

· korta beslutsvägar och nära samarbete i ett engagerat team med miljöfokus

· stor frihet att forma rollen utifrån din kompetens och dina intressen

· flexibilitet att organisera arbetet utifrån uppdragens behov och din livssituation

· möjlighet att påverka företagets fortsatta utveckling

· goda anställningsvillkor, pensions- och försäkringslösningar

Placering och resor

Vi har idag kontor i Borlänge (Borlänge Science Park) och kommer att etablera ett kontor i Östersund under 2027. Beroende på förutsättningar kan det bli aktuellt att etablera kontor på andra orter. Möjligheter finns att utföra delar av arbetet på distans.

Resor och tillfälligt arbete på annan ort ingår i tjänsten.

Ansökan och kontakt

Urval och intervjuer sker löpande. Skicka din ansökan med CV till Magnus Hagström på mejladressen: magnus@hvvm.se

Du är också välkommen att höra av dig om du vill veta mer om rollen.

title: Configuration Management Analyst
description:
This position is listed on behalf of a partner company, who manages all applications and next steps. Our partner is looking for a Configuration Management Analyst based in the United States.

This role is responsible for protecting the integrity, accuracy, and traceability of product data throughout the hardware lifecycle. You’ll own configuration control processes spanning engineering, manufacturing, quality, supply chain, and production. Working hands-on with Arena PLM, you’ll manage bills of materials, revisions, item masters, lifecycle phases, and engineering change processes. You’ll help ensure teams work from a consistent and reliable source of truth as hardware moves from design through production and flight. The role also provides an opportunity to support configuration baselines for flight and safety-critical systems and contribute to audit readiness. It is a remote position with approximately 25% travel and offers the opportunity to work on advanced space hardware programs.

Accountabilities:

  • Own configuration control within Arena PLM, administering item masters, bills of materials, revisions, lifecycle phases, and engineering change objects such as ECOs, ECRs, and deviations.

  • Manage the document and engineering change process by processing, routing, tracking, and coordinating requests and orders through review and approval.

  • Collaborate with engineering, manufacturing, quality, supply chain, and production stakeholders to ensure configuration changes are accurately implemented and traceable.

  • Maintain the integrity of product data by auditing part numbers, revisions, BOM structures, and related records for accuracy, consistency, and completeness.

  • Identify and resolve configuration discrepancies proactively before they result in manufacturing, quality, or production issues.

  • Support Engineering Review Board and Configuration Control Board meetings by preparing document packages, coordinating materials, tracking action items, publishing minutes, and maintaining change logs.

  • Develop, maintain, and enforce configuration management procedures, work instructions, naming conventions, and numbering standards in alignment with applicable industry practices such as AS9100.

  • Establish and maintain traceability across as-designed, as-built, and as-flown configuration baselines, with particular attention to flight and safety-critical hardware.

  • Train and support engineers, buyers, production personnel, and other stakeholders on Arena workflows and configuration management processes.

  • Serve as a key internal resource for PLM-related questions and help teams follow configuration control disciplines effectively.

  • Support internal audits, customer reviews, and regulatory or compliance inspections by preparing accurate configuration and change-management records.

  • Help continuously improve configuration management processes and contribute to a culture of data accuracy, accountability, and operational discipline.

    • Requirements:

    • 5+ years of experience in configuration management, engineering data management, document control, PLM administration, or a closely related field.

    • Bachelor’s degree in engineering, a technical discipline, or equivalent relevant experience.

    • Hands-on experience administering Arena PLM, with the ability and willingness to quickly develop advanced expertise in the platform.

    • Strong understanding of configuration management principles, including BOM structures, revision control, engineering change processes, lifecycle management, and configuration baselines.

    • Familiarity with established configuration management standards and industry practices.

    • Exceptional attention to detail and the ability to work accurately with large volumes of technical and product data.

    • Strong organizational and analytical skills, with the ability to identify discrepancies and maintain accurate records throughout complex product lifecycles.

    • Clear communication skills and the ability to collaborate effectively with both technical and non-technical stakeholders.

    • Ability to enforce process discipline constructively while maintaining efficient workflows and avoiding unnecessary bottlenecks.

    • Experience in a hardware or aerospace startup environment is strongly preferred.

    • Experience supporting data migrations or PLM system implementations, including launching, restructuring, or reconfiguring a PLM environment, is a plus.

    • Exposure to ERP/MRP systems and an understanding of how these systems interact with PLM processes is beneficial.

    • Familiarity with drawing and model-based definition practices is advantageous.

    • Previous experience supporting satellite, launch vehicle, or other space hardware programs is a plus.

    • Candidates must be U.S. citizens, lawful permanent residents of the United States, or protected individuals as defined by 8 U.S.C. 1324b(a)(3), in accordance with U.S. Government space technology export regulations.

      • Benefits:

      • Salary range of $85,000–$100,000 per year for the remote position.

      • Fully remote work within the United States.

      • Approximately 25% travel required.

      • Paid holidays and sick time.

      • Unmetered vacation.

      • Health and dental insurance plans with an 80% employer contribution.

      • 401(k) plan with 4% company matching and immediate vesting.

      • Life insurance.

      • Voluntary short-term and long-term disability coverage.

      • Opportunity to contribute to advanced space hardware programs and products designed for critical missions.

      • Cross-functional exposure across engineering, manufacturing, quality, supply chain, and production.

description:
Idaho National Laboratory (INL) is is seeking an intern to support the Infrastructure Transformation Program by researching and preserving historical site infrastructure. The role involves reviewing original construction plans from early US Navy and National Reactor Testing Station operations, locating and documenting former building sites and utilities, and interpreting civil engineering drawings. The intern will digitize historical materials into EDMS for long-term accessibility and collaborate with the team to verify findings.

This team works a 9x80 schedule onsite at our Idaho Falls Campus. You will also travel between INL facilities. Start date and duration of internship vary based on project and student availability. You may be eligible for course credit for this internship.

Company:

One of the UK's leading Apprenticeship Training Providers is recruiting an Independent End Point Assessor to join their Data & AI delivery team.


This is a full time, permanent position which is fully remote and home based.


They believe in people-powered transformation because they know that all transformation starts with people. They are a professional learning organisation that upskills people, uplifts cultures and future-proofs organisations in a fast-moving world. They design and deliver interactive learning experiences in data, AI, business analysis and technology, including apprenticeships and professional qualifications, many of which maximise UK Government future skills funding.


What you'll do:

As an Independent End Point Assessor, you will assess apprentices against the requirements of three technical standards and make robust, evidence-based grading decisions. You will:

  • Assess project reports, presentations, professional discussions and technical tests, and grade to pass, merit or distinction against the published criteria.

  • Maintain consistency and standardisation across assessments, contributing to standardisation activities and moderation.

Technical experience required:

This is a technical role. You will be assessing at Level 5 through Level 7, so you need genuine hands-on depth across some or all of the following:

  • Data engineering: building and maintaining data pipelines, ETL/ELT, SQL, cloud data platforms (for example Azure, AWS or GCP), tools such as dbt, Databricks, Airflow, Snowflake or BigQuery.
  • Machine learning: designing, training, deploying and monitoring models in production, Python, and the ML lifecycle including MLOps.
  • Applied AI: modern AI and generative AI techniques, responsible AI, and evaluating AI systems.

Desirable qualifications and experience:

  • Assessor qualifications (A1, TAQA, CAVA, or D32/D33), or a willingness to work towards them.
  • Familiarity with apprenticeship standards and end point assessment processes.
  • Previous EPA, assessing, coaching or teaching experience in a technical setting.

title: Mechatronics Engineer II
description:
## **Job Details**

New ideas are all around us, but only a few will change the world. That’s our focus at JPL. We ask the biggest questions, then search the universe for answers—literally. We build upon ideas that have guided generations, then share our discoveries to inspire generations to come. Your mission—your opportunity—is to seek out the answers that bring us one step closer. If you’re driven to discover, create, and inspire something that lasts a lifetime and beyond, you’re ready for JPL.

Located in Pasadena, California, JPL has a campus-like environment situated on 177 acres in the foothills of the San Gabriel Mountains and offers a work environment unlike any other: we inspire passion, foster innovation, build collaboration, and reward excellence.

This unique opportunity is part of the **Mechanical and Control Systems Division (35)**, which creates advanced mechanical, robotics, thermal, propulsion, onboard GNC, and electronic packaging systems. Division 35 develops hardware and systems from early architecture through design, fabrication, subsystem, and system-level integration and test.

You will be working as a _**Mechatronics Engineer**_ within the **Mechanical Engineering, Integration, and Test Section**, which leads the design, analysis, development, integration, and test of flight mechanical and robotic systems for spacecraft, payloads, and ground-based systems. In this role, you will:

- Develop mechanisms, materials, and electronics, including actuators, sensors, controllers, structures, and moving mechanical assemblies, for current and future JPL missions.
- Support mechanical hardware development and mechanical systems engineering activities for payloads, instruments, and spacecraft during all mission phases including proposal, concept/system architecture development, detailed design, integration & test (I&T), and flight operations.
- Perform design and analysis, generate and maintain engineering documentation, and participate in the build and delivery of mechanical engineering products for spaceflight missions.
- Ensure that delivered products meet all technical requirements and programmatic commitments.
- Contribute to cost and schedule estimation and implementation planning of engineering components.
- Support and present at team, line management, and subsystem level technical reviews.
- Provide technical guidance to support engineers, designers, and structural analysts.
- Contribute to the mentorship and training of junior technical team members.
- Perform tasks under the direction of the group supervisor, project management, and project technical leads, work independently and within a team environment, and collaborate on tasks that span a spectrum of disciplines.

**Required Skills:**

- Bachelor’s degree in Mechanical Engineering or related technical discipline with a minimum of 3 years of related experience; or a Master’s degree with a minimum 1 year related experience or PhD in similar disciplines.

- Experience with spacecraft or instrument mechatronics development and/or mechanical hardware design, fabrication, integration, and test.
- Knowledge and experience translating design and performance requirements into electro-mechanical hardware configurations and development plans.
- Experience with task planning, managing schedules and deliverables, and meeting commitments.

**Desired Skills:**

- Demonstrated experience with mechanisms, actuators, sensors, and motor controller technologies.
- Knowledge and experience in electrical engineering and software development for embedded systems.
- Experience developing and delivering spaceflight hardware or other relevant spaceflight project experience.
- Practical experience using CAD modeling software (preferably Unigraphics/Siemens NX, SolidWorks, and Teamcenter) used in a Product Delivery Management (PDM) or similar Concurrent Engineering environment.
- Practical experience performing analysis of mechanical elements using classical hand-calculation methods or Finite Element Analysis (FEA).
- Knowledge of Standards for Geometric Dimensioning and Tolerancing (GD&T) per American Society of Mechanical Engineers (ASME) Y14.5.
- Ability to develop innovative solutions and/or troubleshoot design and implementation challenges.
- Knowledge of academic and industry practices and standards across a range of applications related to the development, analysis, production, testing, verification, and safety of spaceflight hardware and systems.
- Experience managing, implementing, and verifying project and institutional requirements at the subsystem or system levels.
- Experience working across organizations and subject areas, and with outside companies and vendors.
- Excellent verbal and written communication skills.
- Excellent collaboration skills and ability to work across subject areas and organizations.

This includes a variety of health, dental, vision, wellbeing, and retirement plans, paid time off, learning, rideshare, childcare, flexible schedule, parental leave and many more. Our focus is on work-life balance, and living healthy, fulfilling lives as we Dare Mighty Things Together. title: Senior Critical Operations Technician (Australia)
description:
Company Overview

STACK Infrastructure builds, owns, and operates hyperscale and colocation data centers that power the world’s most ambitious technology companies. With a rapidly expanding footprint across APAC, STACK combines deep development expertise, flexible capital, and operational discipline to deliver critical digital infrastructure at scale.

Our clients include the largest hyperscale cloud platforms. We are building a regional platform defined by speed of delivery, power reliability, and long-term partnership — and we are assembling the team to lead that effort.

Summary/Objective

The Senior Critical Operations Technician is the senior on-shift technical role responsible for ensuring safe, stable and consistent operation of critical electrical, mechanical, cooling, controls and life-safety systems. The role provides elevated technical capability, supports first-response incident actions, verifies plant condition after maintenance or resets and guides technicians in executing operational tasks with accuracy and discipline.

The role applies strong operational judgement, trend awareness and structured troubleshooting to stabilise plant conditions within authorised boundaries. The Senior Critical Operations Technician also enhances shift performance by coaching team members and refining documentation quality.

This role directly supports STACK’s commitment to 100% uptime and a concierge-level customer service experience, ensuring risk is proactively managed, planned works are executed safely, and customer communications are clear, timely and professional.

Essential Functions

Reasonable accommodations may be made to enable individuals with disabilities to perform these essential functions.

Critical Operations

• Support STACK’s 100% uptime objective through disciplined operational control, proactive monitoring and accurate technical response.

• Maintain real-time awareness of plant condition through BMS/EPMS, alarms and inspections, taking timely actions within authorised limits.

• Provide senior technical support to shift technicians, assisting with prioritisation, procedural clarity and execution quality.

• Operate and monitor critical electrical and/or mechanical systems, including UPS, PDUs, switchboards, generators, CRAC/CRAH, CDU/FWU, chilled water systems, pumps and associated plant, strictly within approved procedures and authorisations.

• Perform structured diagnostics on abnormal conditions, apply permitted stabilisation actions and escalate with clear technical detail and recommended next steps.

• Support operational event response, including immediate containment actions, technical communication and accurate event documentation.

• Conduct enhanced rounds, including thermal, capacity, vibration/noise, leak-detection and set-point verification, ensuring findings are recorded and actioned.

• Identify trends, weak signals and reliability concerns using BMS/EPMS data and provide recommendations to prevent recurrence.

• Manage on-shift work execution with strict adherence to permit-to-work controls, isolations/LOTO, vendor access and operational handbacks.

• Coordinate vendor activities during shift, ensuring safe execution, clear understanding of plant impacts and thorough return-to-service verification.

• Validate operational readiness following maintenance, resets or configuration changes, confirming alarms, redundancy, load paths and expected operating conditions.

• Review and improve the quality of shift logs, event notes, CMMS entries and handovers to ensure accuracy, clarity and traceability.

• Raise and escalate recurring defects, reliability risks and improvement opportunities through appropriate channels.

• Contribute to procedure reviews, readiness activities, drills and documentation improvements with practical, shift-based insights.

• This role does not perform licensed electrical, mechanical or refrigeration work. All trade-restricted activities are completed by appropriately qualified and licensed personnel. The Senior Critical Operations Technician focuses on operational system management, first-response stabilisation, verification and coordination.

People

• Set a high standard for safety behaviour, operational discipline and professional conduct across the shift.

• Support technicians through on-the-job coaching, demonstrations and constructive feedback to improve capability and consistency.

• Assist with onboarding and familiarisation of new team members, reinforcing authorised boundaries and operational expectations.

• Strengthen team communication by ensuring clear handovers, accurate escalation details and calm coordination during events.

• Participate actively in briefings, toolbox talks, training and operational discussions, offering practical observations and improvement ideas.

• Build collaborative relationships with Security, Projects and vendor personnel to support safe, coordinated site operations.

• Demonstrate a concierge-level customer service approach in all interactions with customers, visitors and stakeholders.

Competencies

• Strong operational discipline and sound judgement in a critical facility environment.

• High technical capability in electrical and/or mechanical systems within authorised boundaries.

• Effective structured troubleshooting and stabilisation capability under pressure.

• Ability to interpret alarms, telemetry, trends and technical documentation.

• Proficiency with BMS/EPMS, CMMS and operational workflow tools.

• Strong written and verbal communication for shift documentation, incidents and customer updates.

• Contractor coordination skills with strong permit-to-work and LOTO awareness.

• Ability to coach others and improve team execution quality.

• Calm, methodical approach during alarms and operational events.

• Continuous improvement mindset focused on reliability and operational quality.

Work Environment / Conditions

• The role operates on a 24/7 rotating shift roster, including nights, weekends and public holidays.

• Work occurs in data halls, plant rooms, electrical/mechanical spaces and external plant areas; PPE is required under site policy.

• Participation in emergency response activities and incident exercises is required.

Travel Required

• Minimal travel expected; occasional travel between local STACK facilities may be required based on operational needs.

Preferred Education and Experience

• Experience in critical environments such as data centres, hospitals, utilities, Defence or industrial facilities.

• Demonstrated capability operating and monitoring critical power and cooling systems, including UPS, generators, switchgear, PDUs/PMMs, ATS/STS, CRAC/CRAH, chilled water systems, pumps, controls and fire systems.

• Hands-on experience conducting operational inspections and first-response stabilisation actions.

• Experience using BMS/EPMS and CMMS/workflow tools for monitoring, work management and operational documentation.

• Ability to read and interpret single-line diagrams, technical drawings and OEM documentation.

• Familiarity with permit-to-work, isolations/LOTO and basic operational risk assessment.

• Strong written and verbal communication suitable for logs, handovers and customer-facing updates.

Additional Eligibility Requirements

• Completion of STACK onboarding and required safety/compliance training.

• Ability to meet site authorisation requirements for system operation and system access.

• Physical capability to perform inspections, rounds and emergency response tasks.

• Ongoing compliance with STACK policies, procedures and behavioural standards.

Work Authorisation/Security Clearance Requirements

• Legal entitlement to work in Australia.

• Ability to satisfy pre-employment screening requirements, as applicable, including right-to-work checks, background checks and reference checks.

• Ability to meet data centre security requirements, including badging, access control and adherence to customer-mandated security protocols.

• Security clearance is not required unless specified for a customer-specific facility.

Equal Opportunity Employer

STACK provides equal employment opportunities to all employees and applicants for employment and prohibits discrimination and harassment of any type without regard to race, colour, religion, age, sex, national origin, disability status, genetics, protected veteran status, sexual orientation, gender identity or expression, or any other characteristic protected by applicable federal, state or local laws.

This policy applies to all terms and conditions of employment, including recruitment, hiring, placement, promotion, termination, redundancy, recall, transfer, leaves of absence, compensation and training.

Other Duties

title: Principal Advanced SVT & FA Engineer
description:

title: Data Scientist  (3651)
description:
Data Scientist (3651) - Monument Place

Data Scientist
Location: Hybrid, Monument Place
Reporting to: Insights Lead

Help Shape the Future of Data-Driven Decision Making at GTR

Are you passionate about turning complex data into meaningful insight that drives real-world outcomes?

At GTR, we're looking for an ambitious and forward-thinking Data Scientist to help us unlock the power of data, machine learning and advanced analytics across one of the UK's largest train operating companies.

This is a unique opportunity to play a key role in establishing GTR's first in-house machine learning capability, helping us better understand future risks, opportunities and operational outcomes. You'll work at the heart of our Data & AI function, developing predictive models that support smarter decision making, improve performance and create tangible value for our customers and business.

About the Role

As a Data Scientist in the Central Data & Ai function, you will use advanced analytics, statistical modelling and machine learning techniques to extract forward-looking insights from large and complex datasets across multiple business domains.

Working closely with operational and business stakeholders, you'll help define business problems, test hypotheses and develop predictive and prescriptive models that influence decision making across commercial, operational and safety functions.

This role offers the opportunity to work within a modern enterprise data environment, leveraging over 40 DataHub products that support more than 2,000 active users. As GTR continues to expand its data and AI capabilities, you'll play an important role in shaping standards, approaches and best practices for data science across the organisation.

What You'll Be Doing

  • Developing predictive and prescriptive models using curated DataHub datasets.
  • Applying statistical and machine learning techniques to identify trends, risks and future outcomes.
  • Working with stakeholders to frame business challenges, define hypotheses and design effective interventions.
  • Translating complex analytical findings into clear, actionable insights for technical and non-technical audiences.
  • Explaining model assumptions, limitations and risks to support informed decision making.
  • Collaborating with Data Engineers to develop data models that support analytical and machine learning use cases.
  • Monitoring, evaluating and improving model performance as business conditions evolve.
  • Contributing to the development of data science standards, governance and best practice across GTR.
  • Supporting the responsible adoption of AI and advanced analytics within an enterprise environment.

What We're Looking For

We're looking for a curious and commercially aware Data Scientist who combines strong technical expertise with excellent stakeholder engagement skills.

You Will Bring:

  • Demonstrable experience delivering end-to-end data science solutions in a business environment.
  • Strong knowledge of statistical modelling, machine learning and predictive analytics techniques.
  • Advanced Python and SQL skills, with experience building scalable analytical solutions for production environments.
  • Experience designing, training, validating and deploying machine learning models.
  • Strong problem-solving capabilities, with the ability to translate complex business challenges into structured analytical approaches.
  • Experience working with large enterprise datasets and integrating multiple data sources to generate actionable insight.
  • Strong data visualisation and storytelling skills, ideally using Power BI or similar tools.
  • Experience working within cloud-based analytics platforms, ideally Microsoft Fabric, Azure, Databricks, Synapse or similar technologies.
  • The ability to communicate complex technical concepts clearly and confidently to stakeholders at all levels.
  • A collaborative mindset with the confidence to challenge assumptions and propose innovative solutions.

Qualifications

  • Degree in Data Science, Computer Science, Statistics, Mathematics or a related discipline, or equivalent practical experience.

Why Join Us?

title: At Your Service Center Associate, Downey Stonewood Center - Part Time
description:
Be Part of an Amazing Story

Macy’s is more than just a store. We’re a story. One that’s captured the hearts and minds of America for more than 160 years. A story about innovations and traditions…about inspiring stores and irresistible products…about the excitement of the Macy’s 4th of July Fireworks, and the wonder of the Thanksgiving Day Parade. We’ve been part of memorable moments and milestones for countless customers and colleagues. Those stories are part of what makes this such a special place to work.

Job Overview

As an At Your Service Center Colleague, you are at the heart of delivering a seamless and personalized shopping experience. You’ll support all At Your Service activities, including Buy Online Pickup In Store (BOPS), merchandise returns, order pickups, and other assigned tasks - all while upholding Macy’s service standards.

This role goes far beyond just being a cashier. Here, the customer is at the heart of everything we do - every day, all day. If you're passionate about selling, reaching goals, working as a team, and creating amazing experiences through genuine hospitality, this could be the perfect fit for you! You’ll also help keep the shopping space clean, organized, and inviting so every customer feels welcome the moment they walk in.

How Our At Your Service Colleagues Spend Their Day…

  • Every day starts with a positive example. As an At Your Service Colleagues (AYS), you come in energized and ready to make an impact - wearing your name badge with pride, greeting teammates with warmth, and helping ensure the At Your Service areas is clean, organized, and ready for customers. You help set the pace by reviewing sales goals, learning about new arrivals and top-selling items, and staying up to date on trends and promotions - so you’re prepared to support the team and engage customers confidently.
  • In the At Your Service area, you lead through action - welcoming customers with genuine hospitality, making eye contact, and starting friendly, personal conversations that build lasting relationships. Assist customers in all aspects of total store fulfillment, including By Online and Pick Up in Store, be proficient in all systems needed to complete transactions, and ensure the collection area is organized so the customer pick-up experience is friction-free
  • You help maintain a shoppable space by recovering merchandise and keeping the pickup and return areas clean while ensuring timely completion and curbside delivery of Buy Online Pickup In Store (BOPS) orders.
  • They always Finish Strong - sharing our Loyalty program benefits, making sure customers have all they need, and ending with a sincere thank-you, often walking the package around and using the customer’s name.
  • We believe service starts with each other - supporting one another with honesty, care, and collaboration so we can better serve our customers and communities.
  • And we know that excellence is a journey - we strive to improve every day, take pride in our work, achieve sales goals and learn from each other to deliver individual and store results.

Full-time colleagues are typically scheduled to work 30 or more hours per week, while part-time colleagues are typically scheduled 12-24 hours per week. All schedules contain weekend shifts as part of the requirements. Hours are dependent on business needs and colleague availability. Information regarding hours per week needed for benefit eligibility purposes can be found here.

Who You Are

  • Flexible availability, including days, evenings, weekends and holidays with regular, dependable attendance and punctuality
  • Must be able to:
    • Understand and communicate effectively with customers, co-workers, and supervisors
    • Read and understand employment policies and safety rules/procedures in English
  • Makes prompt, sound decisions in real time to effectively address customer needs and resolve issues
  • Be comfortable communicating and collaborating with customers and colleagues
  • Meeting daily sales goal challenges
  • Responsible for acquiring new customers by opening credit accounts and sharing loyalty benefits
  • Enjoy meeting people, learning about them, and sharing information
  • Resourceful and eager to start a new venture and can adapt to changing priorities; you can work on your own but are great with team dynamics
  • You can handle electronic devices with no problem

Essential Physical Requirements You Will Perform

  • This position requires talking, lifting, constant moving, standing, and reaching with arms and hands.
  • Standing for at least two consecutive hours, lifting at least 25lbs. stooping, kneeling, crouching, and climbing ladders, reaching, including above eye level.
  • Requires close vision, color vision, depth perception, and focus adjustment.
  • Frequent use of computers and other technology, necessary to perform job functions, including handheld equipment, cash register and ability to process register transactions.

What We Can Offer You

Join a team where work is as rewarding as it is fun! We offer a dynamic, inclusive environment with competitive pay and benefits. Enjoy comprehensive health and wellness coverage and a 401(k) match to invest in your future. Prioritize your well-being with paid time off and eight paid holidays. Grow your career with continuous learning and leadership development. Plus, build community by joining one of our Colleague Resource Groups and make a difference through our volunteer opportunities.

Some additional benefits we offer include:

  • Merchandise discounts
  • Performance-based incentives
  • Annual merit review
  • Employee Assistance Program with mental health counseling and legal/financial advice

Access the full menu of benefits offerings here.

About Us

This is a great time to join Macy’s! Whether you’re helping a customer find the perfect gift, streamlining operations in one of our distribution centers, enhancing our online shopping experience, buying in-style and on-trend merchandise to outfit our customers, or designing a balloon for the Thanksgiving Day Parade, we offer unique opportunities to be part of some of the most memorable moments in people’s lives.

Join us and help write the next chapter in our story - Apply Today!

title: Site Director
description:
Valkyrie Clinical Trials (VCT), a Flourish Research Company, is a leading Oncology multi-site clinical research network with expertise in Oncology research. VCT approaches clinical research with a deep sense of humanity, compassion, and sincere kindness. VCT was founded by leading Clinical Oncologist, Dr. David Berz, and has multiple sites spanning California in Century City, Panaroma City, and Murrieta, and has recently expanded to Denver, Colorado.

Flourish Research is one of the industry’s most progressive and diversified clinical trial organizations, with strong capabilities across cardiology, metabolic disorders, renal, oncology, CNS, pulmonology, and vaccine research. At Flourish Research, we strive toward excellence. In clinical trials and healthcare, excellence means everyone deserves the best care, regardless of their race, color, gender identity, religion, ethnicity, physical abilities, age, sexual orientation, or veteran status. We embrace employees, customers, and patients from these underrepresented groups to help make this vision a reality. Flourish is committed to a safe work environment where all employees, customers, and patients are included, and treated with dignity and respect. The more diversity we have in our team, the more unique perspectives, and ideas we share, and the better prepared we are to serve our communities. WE SEE YOU. WE ARE YOU. WE EMBRACE YOU. WE CELEBRATE YOU!


We are actively hiring a Site Director to support our Valkyrie Clinical Trials San Diego, CA site.

LOCATION: Onsite, San Diego, CA
FLSA: Exempt
HOURS: Monday to Friday, Day Shift, 40 hours per week
Compensation:

ESSENTIAL JOB FUNCTIONS:

Operational Leadership & Site Management

A. Oversee day-to-day oncology site operations, ensuring compliance with FDA, ICH-GCP, and sponsor protocols.

B. Implement and monitor operational and financial metrics including study volume, capacity planning, margins, and productivity.

C. Lead development, execution, and continuous improvement of SOPs aligned with Flourish Research and oncology-specific requirements.

D. Ensure high-quality study conduct, patient safety oversight, and robust PI/Sub-I engagement.

E. Partner with Quality and Risk to achieve strong audit outcomes and uphold data integrity.

Financial & Business Management

A. Own the oncology site P&L; manage to margin/EBITDA targets.

B. Develop and implement growth strategies to expand study volume, diversify oncology indications, and strengthen site competitiveness.

C. Partner with Business Development to maintain sponsor relationships and attract new studies.

D. Support financial budgeting, forecasting, and resource planning.

Oncology Strategy & Market Growth

A. Leverage oncology market trends and sponsor pipelines to shape site strategy.

B. Strengthen partnerships with oncology practices, referral networks, and community physicians.

C. Contributes competitive positioning within the oncology site network landscape.

Team Leadership & Culture

A. Recruit, mentor, and develop clinical and operational staff with oncology expertise.

B. Champion patient-centered, mission-driven culture aligned with Flourish core values.

C. Collaborate closely with investigators and medical leadership to support high-acuity oncology trials.

Technology, Systems & Integration

A. Implement and optimize clinical systems, CTMS platforms, and workflow automation.

B. Support integration across HR, IT, Quality, and Finance when applicable.

C. Standardize processes and performance dashboards to drive operational excellence.

Regulatory, Quality & Compliance

A. Maintain site-level adherence to GCP, ICH, FDA regulations, HIPAA, and oncology-specific safety requirements.

title: Cost Estimator
description:
Why Join Ford of Mexico?

Celebrating over 100 years of legacy in Mexico, we are more than just a business we are a vibrant, collaborative community of over 14,000 innovators shaping the global future of transportation. At Ford, we build what matters, grow where it counts, and drive progress with heart. Whether you are collaborating at our state-of-the-art Global Technology and Business Center (GTBC) or manufacturing iconic, award-winning vehicles in our world-class plants, you will find a culture evolving together, built on trust, passion, and shared purpose. Here, your work moves people forward, and your growth is personal. Join us, and let’s build what’s next together.

In this position...

Product Development uses design thinking & user experience methods to deliver breakthrough products and services that delight our customers. We bring innovative, exciting, and sustainable ideas to life. We have opportunities around the world for you to contribute to advancements in autonomy, electrification, smart mobility technologies, and more!

Cost Estimating (CE) is a function of Global Material Cost as part of Product Development.

Behind every vehicle that rolls off the line are a thousand decisions about cost, value, and efficiency, decisions that determine whether an idea becomes an affordable, profitable, world-class product.

We're looking for a Cost Engineer who doesn't just crunch numbers, but who sees the story behind them: the supplier negotiation that saved program millions, the material substitution that improved margin without compromising quality, the forecast that gave leadership the confidence to greenlight the next big launch.

If you're the kind of person who gets energized by solving complex puzzles, who can translate spreadsheets into strategy, and who wants your analysis to directly influence vehicles driven by millions of people — this role was built for you.

What you'll do...

  • Serve as the financial conscience of vehicle programs by developing, analyzing, and validating should-cost models, piece-part costing, and total cost of ownership analyses for Brake Lines & Tubes and Brake Hoses components, as well as related tooling, design changes, capital investment, and program volume changes.
  • Turn data into actionable decisions, partnering with engineering, manufacturing, and supply chain teams to uncover cost-reduction opportunities for underbody brake components without compromising quality, safety, or performance.
  • Shape supplier strategy by building detailed cost breakdowns and benchmarking analyses for brake lines, tubes, and hoses that equip negotiators with the insight needed to secure the best value from the supply base.
  • Challenge the status quo through competitive teardown and benchmarking studies, physically and analytically disassembling competitor vehicles and brake components to compare materials, manufacturing processes, and design choices—then presenting clear, defensible cost comparisons that shape design decisions before they are locked in.
  • Build and defend should-cost models from the ground up (materials, labor, tooling, overhead, logistics) for Ford-purchased brake parts to validate supplier quotes and strengthen negotiation leverage, while running head-to-head cost-technology comparisons (e.g., different materials or manufacturing methods) to guide engineering toward the best total-cost solution.
  • Bridge finance and engineering as part of the Underbody Cost Estimation team, acting as the translator between technical teams and business leaders to ensure all stakeholders understand the cost implications of design and sourcing decisions for brake lines, tubes, and hoses—including through participation in GEMBA activities to benchmark supplier processes.
  • Bachelor of Industrial Engineering or similar.
  • English advanced.
  • Manufacturing processes knowledge (Tube Fabrication, Hose Extrusion, Plastic Injection, Steel Stamping, Plating, Coating, Brazing, Final Assembly)
  • Capable of interpreting technical drawings (ED&T) and 3D visualization models.

Others: Lean Manufacturing principles and Analytical and Problem-Solving Skills are desired.

Additional Skills:

Team working mindset, data driven, analytical, proactive, effective communication.

Ford of Mexico is committed to being an equal opportunity employer. We believe that a diverse and inclusive workplace is essential to our success. We do not discriminate based on race, religion, color, national origin, gender, sexual orientation, age, marital status, pregnancy, veteran status, or disability status.

Our focus is to build the best team. If you think you can bring value to Ford, love to collaborate, prioritize and aim to deliver excellence in everything you do, we encourage you to apply!

We thank all candidates for their interest, but only those selected for an interview will be contacted.

title: Associate Dietitian
description:
PURPOSE AND SCOPE:

A Registered Dietitian in training with less than the one year of clinical experience will work directly with a qualified dietitian. With direct supervision of a qualified renal dietitian, this position will provide nutritional services for the facilities in-center patients in order to gain the experience required by CMS until year of clinical experience is completed to become a qualified dietitian.


Actively participates in process improvements activities to enhance the likelihood that patients will achieve their individualized patient-specific goals as determined by the patient’s physician. The Dietitian in training would not be qualified to complete patient assessments, develop plans of care, or take responsibility for QAPI program review. Under direct supervision of a company Registered Dietitian (employee with a minimum of 3 years’ experience as a renal dietitian). Adheres to the FMCNA Compliance Program, including following all regulatory and FMS policy requirements. Supports the FMCNA commitment to the Quality Enhancement Program (QEP). Supports FMCNA’s mission, vision, core values and customer service philosophy.


PRINCIPAL DUTIES AND RESPONSIBILITIES:

  • Responsible for driving the company culture through values and customer service standards.
  • Accountable for outstanding customer service to all external and internal customers.
  • Develops and maintains effective relationships through effective and timely communication.
  • Take initiative and action to respond, resolve and follow up regarding customer service issues with all customers in a timely manner.
  • Calculates diet prescription according to standards of practice.
  • Evaluates patient’s knowledge of diet and kidney disease.
  • Completion of Nutrition History forms with patients to be used by CMS-qualified dietitian to complete assessments
  • Provides patient specific education to patient/family/caregiver regarding nutritional status, adequacy measures and results, fluid status, and all nutrition related lab parameters pertaining to their disease process, keeping in mind the learning style and preferences of the patient.
  • Reviews nutrition related lab results:
    • Counsels patient and/or caregiver and formulates appropriate action to assist patient in achieving and sustaining an effective nutritional status.
    • Communicates lab results and recommended treatment changes to the interdisciplinary team as appropriate.
    • Communicates with physician and/or facility staff regarding lab results as appropriate.
    • Communicates lab results and recommended treatment changes to providers of patient care in nursing facilities (i.e. hospitals, short term and long-term care facilities).
    • Monitors adherence and response to nutrition therapy. Addresses issues impacting the patient’s ability to achieve the goals
  • Reviews each patient’s albumin level and body weight at least monthly. Identifies malnourished patients as well as patients at risk for malnutrition and works collaboratively with interdisciplinary team to identify appropriate interventions, resources or solutions. Involves patient/family/caregiver in improvement goals.
  • When appropriate, identifies candidates to refer to physician for nutritional supplements as per disease management agreements.
  • Assist with fluid and volume management of patients
  • Provides fluid and sodium education, as appropriate
  • Collaborates with the interdisciplinary team on management and recommendations for mineral metabolism and renal bone disease, anemia and iron status, nutritional status, psychosocial status, vascular access, modality, rehabilitation status and sodium/volume control.
  • Participates in Quality Assessment and Performance Improvement and Plan of Care meetings with a CMS-qualified dietitian
  • Attends all other pertinent staff meetings as applicable.
  • Collaborates with interdisciplinary team, ensuring that all work areas are safe and clean.
  • Collaborates with the interdisciplinary team in pharmacy-related responsibilities including setup, enrollment, and management
  • Participates in lobby days
  • Educates patients in emergency preparedness as it relates to food and nutrition
  • Conducts staff in-services as needed or requested
  • Adheres to FMCNA algorithm and medical record policies
  • Maintains and improves knowledge and skills for a competent and innovative practice.
  • Maintains dietetic registration and continuing education hours as specified by American Dietetic Association and state licensure regulations where applicable.
  • Other Nutrition services duties as assigned
  • Escalates issues to supervisor for resolution, as deemed necessary.
  • Assist with various projects as assigned by direct supervisor.
  • Performs other related duties as assigned.

PHYSICAL DEMANDS AND WORKING CONDITIONS:

  • The physical demands and work environment characteristics described here are representative of those an employee encounters while performing the essential functions of this job. Reasonable accommodations may be made to enable individuals with disabilities to perform the essential functions.
    • The work environment is characteristic of a health care facility with air temperature control and moderate noise levels. May be exposed to infectious and contagious diseases/materials.
    • Day to day work includes desk and personal computer work and interaction with patients, facility staff and physicians.
    • The position may require travel between assigned facilities and various locations within the community. Travel to training clinics as well as regional, Business Unit and Corporate meetings may be required.

SUPERVISION:

  • None

EDUCATION AND REQUIRED CREDENTIALS:

  • Bachelor’s degree in Nutrition or directly related field, Master’s degree preferred
  • Registered Dietitian as per Commission on Dietetic Registration
  • Current State licensure if applicable

EXPERIENCE AND SKILLS:

  • Less than 1 year’s clinical experience.

The rate of pay for this position will depend on the successful candidate’s work location and qualifications, including relevant education, work experience, skills, and competencies.

Rate: $30- $42.69
